out.sellManifest: A broker two jumps ahead pays well for nineteen names and a heading. The convoy still gets through, mostly.
out.sellCaught: You sell it and the buyer talks. Yusuf hears his own manifest quoted back at him on an open channel before you are out of the sector.

yusufRefugeeLane.text: The procession has stalled at a pinch point you happen to know how to open. Yusuf does not ask. He just floats there with the lane map on his screen where you can see it.

out.openLane: You burn the pinch open and hold position while they file through. It takes hours you do not have. Every hull that passes marks your heading as safe.
out.chargeToll: They pay. Of course they pay. Yusuf pays first and loudest so the ones behind him do not have to argue.
out.sealIt: You go through and bring the pinch down behind you. Nothing follows you. Nothing follows them either.

choirDeepPact.text: The Preacher meets you inside the hymn this time, not beside it. «You signed at the shallow end. There is a deeper reading. It costs more of the hull and gives more of the pattern, and I will not pretend the trade is even.»

out.goDeeper: The hymn takes a bite out of the hull and leaves something in the hole that was never manufactured. Your reactor learns a verse.
out.holdHere: «Prudent.» He does not sound disappointed, which is worse. The shallow reading holds, and it pays what it promised.
out.breakIt: You break the signature line by line on an open channel. The Choir hears every word of it, and the nearest Cantor comes to collect the difference.

preacherFinale.text: The Preacher is waiting at the last quiet station before the Core, and for once he is not performing. «Whatever you decided about us, you are going in there. I would like to know what you will say when it asks.»

opt.singWithHim: Sing it with him one last time
opt.answerPlainly: Tell him what you will actually say

out.singWithHim: You take the lower line. He takes the higher. For ninety seconds the sector has a shape, and the reactor holds the charge long after the sound stops.
out.answerPlainly: You tell him plainly. He listens the whole way through without correcting a word, and then hands over the plating he was going to be buried in.
out.cutHimOff: You cut him off mid-verse. His acolytes take that about as well as you expected, and they are between you and the Core.

keeperThread.text: The Keeper's relay finds you between beacons. «You have been doing my work. I do not know whether to thank you or bill you. Come to that — what do you want out of this?»

out.repayHim: You send the scrap and the tally of every beacon you touched. He does not thank you. He files it, which for him is the same thing.
out.askMore: He gives you something out of the maintenance stock and does not say another word for two jumps.
out.askMoreCold: He pays you off in salvage rights, cold as vacuum, and stops routing you the easy beacons.
out.logPass: Your log dovetails with his. Two half-maps become one map, and three rows of the lane resolve out of the static.
out.logFail: The transfer corrupts halfway. He gets a broken log and a broken impression, and the tide comes up behind the failed handshake.

hullBreakerYard.text: A breaker yard still running on automatic. It has been cutting the same hull into the same pieces for years, and the pieces are stacked in a way that suggests somebody was still collecting.

out.takeStack: Clean plate, cut to a standard nobody uses any more. It sells anyway.
out.takeStackTrap: The stack was load-bearing. Half the yard comes down across your dorsal.
out.stopTheYard: You kill the bus and the arms sag. Whatever ship that was, it is allowed to stop being cut now.
out.restartPass: You reprogram the cutting order. It starts producing parts you can actually use.
out.restartFail: The arms take your instruction as a target designation.

tugStrike.text: Eleven tugs holding station across the lane, engines cold, transponders reading the same three words: NOT UNTIL PAID.

out.payThem: They open the lane and hand you their route notes, which are better than anything you were flying on.
out.crossPicket: Nobody shoots. Eleven transponders write your registry down at the same moment.
out.haulForThem: You take a load nobody is being paid for. The yards downstream hear about it before you arrive.

salvageQuarantine.text: A quarantine buoy, forty years expired, still politely refusing to let anyone into a debris field it has no authority over.

out.obeyIt: You route around. Whatever it was protecting stays protected for another few decades.
out.breakSeal: Sealed cargo, sealed for a reason that stopped applying decades ago. Mostly.
out.breakSealBad: The reason it was sealed is still in there, and it has had forty years to get hungry.
out.readBuoy: It logged every hull that ignored it. The list is long, and the headings on it are useful.

driftSchool.text: Somebody has been running a school out of a gutted freighter. Nine children, one very tired adult, and a curriculum that is mostly about not dying in a drift field.

out.donate: The tired adult does not thank you. One of the children draws your hull on the bulkhead, badly and permanently.
out.teachThem: You explain lane discipline to nine people who will outlive you. Explaining it out loud fixes something in your own hands.
out.takeTheFreighter: It powers the lights and the air. They will manage. People here usually manage.

clanFuneral.text: A clan is burning one of its own into the field, which out here means opening the hull and letting the drift take her. They have noticed your registry.

out.standDown: You hold station for the full nineteen minutes. Their yardmaster remembers who did that.
out.salvageDrift: The hull she went out in was worth more than the ceremony. Somebody was going to take it.
out.salvageDriftSeen: They left a picket. Of course they left a picket.
out.sendSalute: Nobody out here has heard the old three-tone in thirty years. Two of the clan ships answer it before they think.

coolantBloom.text: A coolant bloom the size of a city block, freezing and re-freezing on a slow cycle. Something is keeping it fed.

out.tapPass: Slow hands, slow valves, no spike. The tanks come back full and the reactor runs cold for a while.
out.tapFail: One valve opens too far and the bloom answers the way pressure always answers.
out.findSource: A hull under the ice, still venting, still running its cycle for a crew that is not aboard.
out.burnIt: It goes up clean and the lane clears for everybody. Whatever was living in it does not get a vote.

manifestAuction.text: An open-channel auction for a cargo manifest nobody has seen. Three bidders, and one of them is bidding in fleet script that stopped being money forty years ago.

opt.haul: Take the unsold lot on consignment

out.bidHigh: The manifest is real. Half of it is already salvaged, and the other half is worth the whole bid.
out.bidHighDud: The cargo is gone. The routes on the manifest are not, and routes out here are almost cargo.
out.backScript: You vouch for the script on an open channel. Somebody's grandmother's pay finally buys something.
out.jamAuction: Nobody wins it. You collect the lot at the reserve price two hours later, from a very annoyed clerk.
out.haul: Nobody bought the coils. The clerk hands them over with a delivery address and no warranty, and the first gun runs a size smaller beside them.

wardenPatrolBoat.text: A Warden patrol boat, one crew, forty years past its rotation. It hails you with a standard stop order and then, after a pause, asks whether the order still means anything.

opt.answerYes: Tell him it still means something

out.answerYes: He runs the full stop-and-inspect, by the book, for the first time in a decade. Then he gives you the patrol grid.
out.answerNo: He is quiet for a while. Then he strips the boat's ordnance and gives it to you, because he will not be needing it.
out.papersPass: Your paperwork is in order in the way only a real salvager's paperwork is. He pays the standing bounty on it.
out.papersFail: He finds the discrepancy in eleven seconds and fines you, apologetically, out of forty years of habit.

wreckedRelayFarm.text: Sixty relay masts in a row, all pointed the same way, all dead. The sixty-first is pointed somewhere else and is drawing power.

out.traceIt: The heading is not on any chart. It is on yours now.
out.stripFarm: Sixty masts of good copper. The sixty-first keeps drawing power the whole time you work.
out.realign: You put it back in line with its sixty siblings. The array wakes up for eleven seconds and says a name.

tetherRace.text: Two haulers have strung a tether across a gap and are betting on who can cross it faster without cutting it. They have space for a third.

out.racePass: You cross clean and the tether is still humming behind you. Both haulers pay without arguing.
out.raceFail: You cut it. Nobody gets paid, and one hauler is now on foot in the most literal sense available out here.
out.betWin: Old hulls know their own tolerances. She crosses like she has done it a thousand times, which she has.
out.betLose: Old hulls also know their own limits, and hers picks today to find one.
out.cutTether: Good line, good winch, and two people who will be telling this story about you for a while.

yusufApprentice.text: Yusuf's apprentice hails you privately. «He will not ask, so I am asking. There is a part he needs and a yard that will not sell to him.»

out.buyIt: He works out where it came from in about four minutes and says nothing about it for the rest of the sector.
out.stealIt: The yard will not miss it for a month. The apprentice will not say where it came from for longer than that.
out.stealItSeen: The yard misses it immediately. You get out with the part and a tail.
out.tellHim: He is angry for about ten seconds and then very carefully not angry. He fixes something on your hull he was not asked to fix.

iceLighter.text: An ice lighter, still under thrust, still empty. Its autopilot has been running the same delivery loop since before the Cut and has never once been told to stop.

opt.loadIt: Load it and let it run

out.loadIt: It accepts the load, logs it, and carries on. Somewhere down the loop, somebody is going to get a delivery.
out.boardIt: Forty years of maintenance on a hull nobody used. Every part comes off clean.
out.stopIt: It acknowledges, cuts thrust, and goes dark in under a second. Forty years, and it took one word.

driftCourt.text: Three hulls have convened a salvage court over a wreck, which out here means shouting at each other on a shared channel until somebody concedes. They want a fourth party to rule.

out.ruleFair: Nobody is happy, which all three of them recognise as the shape of a fair ruling. Your fee is paid in thirds.
out.ruleForSelf: You award the wreck to the only party present with guns, and take a finder's cut off the top.
out.auditPass: The wreck is not what any of them think it is, and your reading settles the argument in four sentences.
out.auditFail: Your survey is wrong in a way all three of them can see, and the shouting resumes with you in it.

driftReputation.text: A hauler out of the Drift Fields matches your vector without being asked. «You are the one who did the decent thing back there. We pass that along.»

out.takeEscort: They fly your flank through the whole Rift and peel off without asking for anything.
out.askCargo: Salvage, mostly. They give you the piece they were arguing about.
out.askCargoEmpty: Nothing. They are running empty and paying you anyway, out of a fund nobody administers.
out.sendThemHome: The Rift is not for haulers. They go, and leave you their charts on the way out.

driftWake.text: Someone has been broadcasting your registry on the Drift Fields band with a short list attached. The list is accurate.

out.jamIt: The band goes quiet. Everything else on it goes quiet too, which people notice.
out.answerIt: You read the list back, item by item, and do not argue with any of it. The band stays quiet for a different reason.
out.findPass: A single relay on a dead hull. Whoever set it up is long gone; the recording is not.
out.findFail: You chase it into a fold and lose two hours and some plating. The broadcast continues.

quietPassage.text: The Rift here is folded so tight that sound arrives before the thing that made it. Your own engine note reaches you from ahead.

out.followTheNote: You fly toward the sound of yourself and come out three rows further along than you should have.
out.cutEngines: The fold has nothing to echo. For eleven minutes nothing at all happens, and the hull uses them.
out.soundPass: The return comes back clean and carries something with it that was not in the fold a moment ago.
out.soundFail: The fold returns your ping forty times, all at once, from every direction.

wardenRelay.text: A Warden relay wakes up as you pass and reads you a duty roster. Every name on it is yours, assigned to posts that no longer exist.

out.acceptPost: You log in against a post that has been empty for forty years. The relay grants you its standing authority, which is nothing and everything.
out.wipeRoster: The roster goes. The relay's memory is worth something intact and more in pieces.
out.copyRoster: Forty years of posts, watches and reliefs. Somebody should have this, and now somebody does.

manifestBuyer.text: The buyer from the Drift Fields auction has found you, which is impressive, because you did not leave a heading.

out.dealAgain: He pays over the odds, twice, and then asks how you like being findable.
out.cutHim: You change your transponder in front of him. It is rude, effective, and he respects both halves.
out.tracePass: A tag on your hull, welded during the auction. You pull it and keep the transmitter.
out.traceFail: You find nothing, which is worse than finding something, and he keeps finding you.

haulerReunion.text: The tether haulers have set up a permanent crossing in the Rift and named it after the crossing you were part of. They want you to cut the ribbon, which here means the first run.

opt.tollIt: Ask for a share of the tolls

out.firstRun: You cross first and the line holds. Eleven hulls follow you through before the hour is out.
out.firstRunRough: The line holds. Your dorsal does not. They pay the difference without being asked.
out.refuseHonour: You tell them to send their oldest hull instead. She crosses, and the crossing gets her name.
out.tollIt: They agree, because they named it after you and cannot now say no. The tolls arrive on time and feel exactly as good as that.

foldedArchive.text: An archive hull, folded into itself so that every corridor leads to the same room. The room has been catalogued nine times, in nine hands.

out.addTenth: You write your own list in your own hand. The fold accepts it and something in the arithmetic loosens.
out.burnThem: Nine catalogues, one fire, one room that finally stops insisting on being described.
out.ninthPass: The ninth hand is recent. Weeks, not decades. It lists an exit the other eight do not.
out.ninthFail: You lose the thread halfway and take the lamp with you when you leave. The tenth catalogue will not be written.

twinTransit.text: Two identical hulls pass you on identical vectors, four seconds apart. Both hail you. Both use your name.

out.answerFirst: The first is grateful and gives you something. The second stops transmitting mid-word.
out.answerSecond: The second knows things about the next four hours that have not happened yet. It shares two of them.
out.answerNeither: You hold silence for eleven minutes. Only one hull comes out the far side of the fold, and it is not on your scope.

riftSurgeon.text: A medical hull, still lit, still sterile, running a surgery bay that has not had a patient in decades. It offers you an appointment.

out.takeIt: Whatever it does to the hull, it does properly, and it logs the procedure under a patient number from before the Cut.
out.takeItOff: It works from a manual for a hull class that no longer exists. Most of the procedure still applies.
out.stripBay: Sterile field emitters keep their value. The hull's lights stay on the whole time you work.
out.bookOther: You broadcast the coordinates and the appointment slots on an open channel. Within the hour, three hulls have booked.

causalDebt.text: A fold offers you a trade with no counterparty: take something now, and the Rift will take something back at a moment of its choosing.

out.takeNow: The thing is in your hold before you finish agreeing. The other half of the trade has not happened yet.
out.payFirst: You open a bulkhead and let it take the plating up front. The books balance and stay balanced.
out.declineIt: Refusing is itself an answer, and the fold files it. The way through opens without a fee.

unlitChapel.text: A Choir chapel with the lights off and the hymn running anyway. The Preacher is not here; a recording of him is, and it is answering questions.

out.askIt: It answers a question you did not ask, correctly, and then answers the one you did.
out.silenceIt: The chapel goes quiet in the middle of a line. Nothing objects, which is somehow the worst part.
out.copyIt: You take a clean recording. It is shorter than it sounded and it does not loop where you expected.

riftPilotage.text: A pilot's guild board, half-burned, still listing rates for lanes that fold differently every year. Somebody has kept it updated by hand.

out.hirePilot: She has flown this fold eleven hundred times and charges as if it were the first.
out.readBoard: The rates say more about the lanes than the charts do. The expensive ones are expensive for a reason.
out.takeBoard: It comes off the bulkhead in one piece. Whoever was updating it is going to arrive and find nothing to update.

echoOfTheCut.text: For eleven seconds every instrument you own agrees on a single reading, and the reading is forty years old.

out.recordIt: Eleven seconds of the Cut, from outside it. Echo listens to it four times and says nothing.
out.ridePass: You match the old reading and hold it. For a moment the Rift treats you as something it has already accounted for.
out.rideFail: You cannot hold it. Whatever the Rift was about to account for, it accounts for the plating instead.
out.shutItOut: Eleven seconds of nothing at all, chosen on purpose. The hull comes out of it steadier than it went in.

processionEscort.text: The haulers who followed you out of the Drift Fields have caught up, and they have brought the whole crossing crew with them into a place none of them should be.

opt.armThem: Arm them and hold the lane

out.sendBack: They argue for four minutes and then go. Somebody leaves a spare pump on your dock on the way out.
out.useThem: Eleven crews stripping a Procession wreck work faster than any yard. Everyone gets paid.
out.useThemCost: It goes well until it does not. Two hulls do not come back and everybody keeps working anyway.
out.armThem: You spend your own scrap on their turrets. The lane behind you stays open for the rest of the sector.

brokerInTheChoir.text: The buyer has taken orders. He is wearing Choir grey now and he still has your registry written on the back of his hand.

out.dealAnyway: The Choir's stock is better than the Rim's and its prices are stranger. He does not haggle any more.
out.buyBackName: He washes his hand in front of you, slowly, and looks genuinely relieved about it.
out.ordersPass: The orders name three hulls and a heading. One of the hulls is yours; the heading is useful.
out.ordersFail: You get halfway through before he notices, and the rest of the page is now a matter of doctrine.

postingOrders.text: A Warden checkpoint in the Procession, staffed by nobody, still issuing transit papers to anyone who asks correctly.

out.useAuthority: The checkpoint recognises the post you are logged against and stamps everything you put in front of it.
out.forgeThem: Blank stock, working stamp, nobody to check. You print more than you need and sell the rest.
out.forgeThemFlag: The stamp logs every impression. Somewhere a very old system starts flagging your registry.
out.openIt: You broadcast the correct phrasing on an open channel. Anyone in the Procession can have papers now.

reliquaryLedger.text: The Choir keeps a ledger of everything it has taken and everything it intends to. Your name is in the second half.

out.strikeName: One line, one stroke, and a doctrine problem that will be somebody's job to solve.
out.readForward: The intentions are specific, dated and mostly on time. It is the most accurate chart you have ever held.
out.copyLedger: You take a copy and put the original back exactly as it was, which takes longer than stealing it.

fieldHospital.text: The surgeon hull's appointment list reached the Procession before you did. Forty hulls are queued at a station that cannot treat them.

opt.fetchSurgeon: Go and fetch the surgeon hull

out.triage: You spend a day sorting forty hulls into three lines. Nobody thanks you and the queue moves.
out.sellPlaces: There is a price for going first and forty hulls willing to discuss it.
out.fetchSurgeon: It comes when called. It has been waiting to be called for a very long time.

debtCollector.text: The Rift's half of your trade has arrived, wearing the shape of a Procession hull and holding out an itemised list.

out.payIt: It takes plating, time and one instrument you liked. The books close and stay closed.
out.disputeIt: Two of the items were never yours. It concedes both, immediately, and looks embarrassed about it.
out.disputeItLose: The list is correct in every line, and disputing it adds a line.
out.outrunIt: You can outrun it. You cannot outrun the arithmetic, but you can put some distance between you and the arithmetic.

twinInTheProcession.text: One of the Procession's hulls is broadcasting your engine note. It has been in the line for years, according to everyone in it.

out.boardIt: The layout is yours down to the cable runs. The log is not, and the log is the interesting part.
out.boardItEmpty: There is nobody aboard and there never was. The engine note keeps playing after you leave.
out.hailIt: You put the question on the Procession's own channel. Four hundred hulls hear the answer, and the answer is your voice.
out.letItRide: Whatever it is, it is holding a place in a line that needs places held.

hymnSchool.text: The Choir is teaching the hymn to children. The Preacher watches you notice, and does not look away.

out.sayNothing: He takes your silence as agreement and gives you the teaching verse, which is not the verse you have been hearing.
out.takeThem: Nine of them come. Two do not, and the two who stay are the reason the Choir will remember your name.
out.arguePass: You find the contradiction in the teaching verse and say it out loud in front of the class.
out.argueFail: He lets you finish, then answers in four words, and one of the children writes them down.

processionCensus.text: Somebody is counting the Procession, hull by hull, and has been for eleven years. They are four hundred short and will not say of what.

opt.tellTruth: Tell them where the four hundred went

out.helpCount: Two days of tallying. The gap closes to three hundred and ninety-one and the counter weeps about it.
out.buyCount: Eleven years of headings, registries and dates. Worth more than the hull that carried it.
out.tellTruth: You have seen enough of the Rift to guess, and your guess is close enough to end eleven years of counting.

acolyteFerry.text: An acolyte is ferrying pilgrims across a dead zone in a hull that will not survive the round trip, and knows it.

out.takeThemOver: Two crossings, forty pilgrims, one hull that holds. They leave you something from the reliquary they were carrying.
out.buyHull: He takes the scrap and walks the pilgrims the long way round, which takes a month and costs nobody anything.
out.letItGo: He makes it. The hull does not make it back, and he is fine with the arithmetic.
out.letItGoBad: He does not make it. You salvage what comes back through, because somebody was going to.

wardenTribunal.text: Three Warden hulls have convened a tribunal over a lane murder from thirty years ago. They are still arguing about jurisdiction.

out.giveJurisdiction: You say the words that make a court a court. They convict in nine minutes and adjourn for thirty years of paperwork.
out.dissolveIt: You point out that none of them has authority and all three of them know it. They dock and sell you their evidence.
out.standWitness: You did not see it happen. You saw the wreck, which is thirty years closer than anybody else got.

haulersAtTheCore.text: The haulers are here. Not near the Core — at it, holding a picket line across the approach so nothing follows you in.

opt.armThemAgain: Give them everything you can spare

out.thankThem: They will hold as long as they can hold. Everyone involved understands what that means.
out.sendThemOff: It takes four minutes of shouting. Eleven hulls turn for home and you go the rest of the way with nobody behind you.
out.armThemAgain: You strip your own hold into their racks. The line holds a great deal longer than anybody expected.

ledgerAtTheThreshold.text: The Choir's ledger is here, open, and the intention written against today's date is a single word: yours.

out.signIt: You write your own name under the Choir's copy of it. Both versions agree from here on.
out.tearPage: The page comes out clean. The Choir does not need the page; it needed you to leave it in.
out.writeSomeoneElse: There is nothing stopping you. Nothing at all. The Choir accepts the substitution without comment.
out.writeSomeoneElseSeen: The name you write is already three lines above, in the same hand as yours.

lastCheckpoint.text: The last Warden post before the Core, and it is manned. One officer, forty-one years on station, asking for papers.

out.showPapers: He reads every line. Then he stamps them, salutes, and gives you the last forty-one years of his log.
out.relieveHim: You use the words. He blinks twice, says «about time», and hands over the whole post before he can think about it.
out.runPost: He does not fire. He logs it, which after forty-one years is the only thing he has left to do about anything.

hospitalConvoy.text: The queue from the Procession followed the surgeon hull all the way here. Forty patients, one theatre, and a Core that is about to make the question moot.

out.buyTime: You stand between forty hulls and whatever is coming out of the Core for as long as the plating lasts.
out.moveThem: Two days of shepherding forty damaged hulls backwards up a lane. They pay you in parts, which is all they have.
out.takeTheatre: One patient, one theatre, one very short queue. The forty are still outside when you undock.

riftAudit.text: Every fold between you and the Core opens onto the same room, and in the room is your account, itemised to the second.

out.acceptAudit: You sign every page without reading it, because you already know what is on them. The folds stop repeating.
out.contestPass: You find the double entry. The Rift has been billing you twice for the same second since Sector Three.
out.contestFail: Every line holds. Contesting an accurate account costs exactly what the account said it would.
out.burnBooks: The room burns. The folds keep opening onto it, burning, over and over, all the way to the Core.

doubleAtTheDoor.text: Your double is at the Core's threshold, holding station, and it has been waiting long enough to have painted a name on its hull. The name is not yours.

out.letItGoFirst: It goes in. Whatever the Core asks, it asks that one first, and the answer arrives back out to you.
out.takeItsName: You paint it on your own hull. It fits. It has always fitted, which is the problem.
out.goTogether: Two hulls, one threshold, one engine note. The Core will have to decide which of you it was expecting.

hymnAtTheEdge.text: The children are singing it here, at the edge, in a hull with no engines. Somebody brought them all this way to be close to it.

out.takeThemHome: Nine of them fit if you cut the hold in half. You cut the hold in half.
out.singWithThem: The hull with no engines has better acoustics than anything the Choir built on purpose.
out.giveThemEngines: You buy them thrust out of your own hold. Whether they use it to leave is not your part of it.

finalCount.text: The counter is here, at the very edge, and the tally is finally complete. Four hundred and eleven names, all in one place, all accounted for.

out.readThemOut: Four hundred and eleven names on an open channel, one at a time, into whatever is listening.
out.keepList: Somebody has to carry it out, and the counter is not going any further than this.
out.burnList: Eleven years of work, gone in nine seconds. The counter watches and does not stop you, which is its own kind of answer.

approachSilence.text: Six hours out from the Core the noise stops. Not the signal — the noise. Every band you own goes flat and clean at once.

out.broadcast: Your voice goes out and does not come back, and something adjusts to make room for it.
out.listenOnly: Six hours of clean silence, recorded in full. Echo asks you to play it back twice.
out.shutDown: You cut every antenna and fly the last six hours blind and quiet, which is the only rest you get.

lastYard.text: A yard has set up in the Core's shadow, run by people who came out here to work and could not think of a reason to leave.

out.refitHere: They work fast and they work well and nobody asks what you are going in there to do.
out.warnThem: Four of them go. The rest stay, and one of them fixes your engines for free out of spite.
out.hireCrew: Three of them sign on, and they are better at your own systems than you are.
out.hireCrewNone: Nobody signs on. They spend your scrap on your hull instead and tell you to come back for them after.

thresholdMarket.text: Somebody is running a stall at the threshold itself. Not Mara — but the prices are hers, and so is the handwriting on the board.

out.buyEverything: It is not much of a stall. What is on it is the last inventory anyone will take out here.
out.askWhose: «She sent the prices ahead,» they say. «Said somebody would come this far and need them fair.»
out.leaveStock: You add what you can spare to the board and price it at cost, in the same handwriting.

derelictLibrary.text: A hull packed floor to ceiling with paper. Somebody spent a working life printing out everything they were afraid of losing.

opt.indexIt: Index it for whoever comes next

out.readSome: Charts, mostly. Charts and one long letter that is not addressed to anybody.
out.readSomeGold: Between two boxes of manifests there is a schematic that was never meant to be printed.
out.takeItAll: Paper burns and paper sells. You choose the second one and fill the hold.
out.indexIt: Four hours of sorting somebody else's fear into alphabetical order. It steadies your hands.

theOtherSalvager.text: Another salvager is working the same wreck from the other side. Neither of you saw the other arrive.

opt.haul: Take his live hold off him

out.splitIt: Half each and both of you out before the tide. It goes better than either of you expected.
out.splitItBetter: They know the hull class and you know the wiring. Together you get to something neither would have found.
out.raceThem: You are faster. They are still cutting when you undock, and they say nothing at all.
out.raceThemLose: They are faster. You take a torch burn across the arm proving otherwise.
out.giveWay: You undock and leave the cut open for them. They log your registry as one of the good ones.
out.haul: He is out of air for them and says so without dressing it up. A hold of sleepers, a station that will take them, and a hull that pays at every node.

frozenBroadcast.text: A distress call, forty years old, still repeating on a loop that has outlived everyone it was for.

out.answerIt: Nobody answers back. The loop stops anyway, which was presumably the point of it.
out.answerItLive: Somebody answers back. Two words, badly compressed, and then nothing for the rest of the sector.
out.triangulate: The source is a hull that is not where the call says it is, and has not been for a long time.
out.killLoop: The transmitter is worth something and the band is worth more. Both are yours in eleven minutes.

debtorsHull.text: A hull with three liens on it and one very tired owner, who has heard that you settle up.

opt.walkOn: Leave the liens where they lie

out.clearOne: One down, two to go, and one owner who now knows exactly where you are going.
out.buyTheHull: Three liens, one signature, one hull you will strip for the one part you actually wanted.
out.buyTheDebt: Now the liens are yours. The owner works for you until they are not, which is a different kind of kindness.
out.walkOn: You wish the owner luck and mean it. The liens stay on the hull, and the owner's eyes stay on your stern.
out.walkOnTender: You leave them to it. A creditor's tender takes your heading, and the lane grows louder behind you.

noSignalDrift.text: A pocket of the lane where nothing propagates. Sensors, comms, even your own hull noise stop at the boundary.

out.feelPass: Dead reckoning, old numbers, steady hands. You come out where you meant to.
out.feelFail: You come out somewhere else, and something in the pocket comes out with you before it lets go.
out.goAround: The long way costs you time you do not have and no plating at all.
out.mapIt: A dead zone with a known edge is worth more than a lane, and every hauler in the sector will buy the edge.

crewPetition.text: Four people you have helped at various points have found each other and drafted something. It is, technically, a petition.

out.readIt: They want to come with you. All four of them. The document runs to two pages of reasons.
out.takeThem: Four more people, four more sets of hands, four more ways this ends badly. Two of them can weld.
out.sendThemOn: You buy them passage the other way and they argue the entire time it takes to arrange.

beaconWake.text: A beacon you have already resolved is transmitting again, and it is transmitting your registry along with everything else.

out.letItSing: Every hull in the sector now knows where the lane is safe and who made it that way.
out.scrubName: The beacon keeps working. It just stops saying who fixed it, which is how you prefer it.
out.boostIt: You spend your own parts making somebody else's beacon louder. The Keeper's network notices within the hour.

interferenceBloom.text: The tide is running early here and it is running through a wreck field, which makes the whole area read as one enormous unstable die.

out.rideSmallPass: Nothing spikes. You cross on the quietest numbers you own and the tide goes out behind you.
out.rideSmallFail: One number comes up loud and the whole field answers it.
out.waitItOut: Six hours of nothing, burned fuel and repairs you had been putting off.
out.pushThrough: You take the field at speed and come out the far side with a hold full of somebody's cargo.
out.pushThroughBad: You take the field at speed and the field takes a strake off your flank for it.

lastLetter.text: A message capsule, launched forty years ago on a heading that would have taken it out of the sector. Something turned it around.

out.readLetter: It is addressed to somebody who was aboard the fleet. It says «do not come back», twice, in two different hands.
out.relaunchIt: You give it thrust and a clean heading out of the sector. Forty years late and still going.
out.keepCapsule: Forty-year-old launch gear, never used twice, in perfect condition. It will fetch a price.

scavengerWake.text: A funeral, if you are generous about the word. Nine scavengers, one hull, and a body they cannot agree on the name of.

out.nameThem: You take a registry off the hull's plate and read it out. Nine people accept it instantly and gratefully.
out.joinWake: Six hours of other people's stories. One of them turns out to be a chart.
out.joinWakeGift: They send you off with the dead one's tools, because nobody else will take them.
out.takeTheHull: They take the offer. They were always going to take the offer. Nobody enjoys the transaction.

rimNoticeboard.text: A physical noticeboard bolted to a docking spar, forty years of paper on it, the top layer dated this week. Most of it is people looking for people.

out.readIt: Two salvage tips, one warning about a lane, and a name you will hear again before the sector is out.
out.readItOld: Under this week there is a salvage claim nobody ever filed. It is still valid, technically.
out.postYours: You write your registry, your heading and one line about what you are looking for. It is the first honest thing you have done all week.
out.stripBoard: Forty years of paper, one plate of good alloy underneath. You take the plate.
out.haul: A shielding-ballast haul: four crates and an address a few rows on. The engines will feel every kilo of it.

hushAntechamber.text: A room of dead space the size of a fleet yard, and no sound reaches into it — not your engines, not the tide. The Keeper's marker floats at its centre, still transmitting, its message eaten one word from the edge.
hushAntechamber.listenOut: Twenty minutes of nothing. Then the shape of the nothing, which is not the same thing, and Echo maps three rows of it before the silence closes again.
hushAntechamber.speakOut: You give it your callsign. It gives you back the marker's salvage rights and a pressure behind the eyes that does not leave.
hushAntechamber.passOut: The long way costs an hour and a little fuel. Echo runs a hull patch with the quiet time and says nothing about it.

retroSalvage.text: A salvage buoy, correctly filed, correctly tagged — with your registry on it. The timestamp is four hours from now. Whatever left it here has not left it yet.
retroSalvage.takeA: Inside is a die you have not bought yet, packed the way you pack things. You decide not to think about the packing.
retroSalvage.takeB: Inside is a hull sample. Yours. Torn, not cut. You seal the buoy again and the tear on your own plating opens on schedule.
retroSalvage.log: File it and sell the coordinates
retroSalvage.logOut: Somebody in the Rim will pay for a buoy that files itself. You let them find out the rest on their own time.
retroSalvage.leaveOut: You log the position and move on. Four hours later Echo notes, without comment, that the buoy is gone.
retroSalvage.haulOut: A keeper's log no keeper has written yet, addressed to a station you have not reached. Carrying it pulls the needle toward order, and it does not ask first.

foldedYard.text: Mara's stall is here. It should not be — you left her nineteen jumps and one act behind. She is restocking, badly, from crates that keep arriving before she orders them.
foldedYard.tradeOut: She welds a plate she says she bought from you last week. The plate is good. You pay and do not argue the calendar.
foldedYard.ask: Ask her how she got here
foldedYard.askOut: «Same way as you. Somebody asked me to stay and I said yes.» She patches you for free and marks your ledger open at every yard past this one.
foldedYard.salvage: Strip the stall while she is turned away
foldedYard.salvagePass: You take the crates that have not been ordered yet. She notices at exactly the wrong time, which out here is also the right one.
foldedYard.salvageFail: The crate you pick is the one she throws. Mara has excellent aim in every direction of time.

ghostFleetSignal.text: Fleet-standard hail, forty years stale, on a channel that was decommissioned before it was built. Yusuf's voice is on it. Yusuf is nineteen jumps behind you and has never been here.
ghostFleetSignal.answerOut: You give them your name and your heading. Twelve carriers acknowledge. Their reactors are still warm on your instruments, and yours borrows from them.
ghostFleetSignal.recordOut: Forty years of a fleet's last hour, clean, in your hold. Someone in the Rim will pay a great deal not to hear it.
ghostFleetSignal.jamOut: The hail stops mid-word. Whatever was riding the carrier stops with it, and the interference in this whole reach drops a step.

causalityAudit.text: A customs drone with no registry hails you for a manifest of the cargo you are going to carry. It is very polite. It has been waiting here for a long time to be polite at somebody.
causalityAudit.submitPass: The numbers agree with a future you have not had yet. The drone stamps everything and hands you a bonded crate as a courtesy.
causalityAudit.submitFail: The numbers do not agree. The drone files a discrepancy, and the whole reach tightens by a notch to accommodate it.
causalityAudit.forge: File a manifest you like better
causalityAudit.forgeOut: You write the cargo you would rather have had. The drone believes you, and pays out the difference in salvage rights.
causalityAudit.refuseOut: «Noted.» It is still polite. It also flags your heading to everything downstream of here, which answers promptly.

quietChoir.text: The Choir got this far. Their hulls are here, arranged in the formation they use for singing, and the formation is holding without any of them alive in it.
quietChoir.sing: Take the empty part and sing it
quietChoir.singOut: The formation accepts you. For two fights afterwards your reactor starts full and something is very pleased about that.
quietChoir.listenOut: It is not a hymn. It is forty years of one held note, and it repairs what it passes through, including you.
quietChoir.cutOut: Four hulls come loose and the note stops. The salvage is good. The stopping is what you will remember.

unwrittenLog.text: A ship's log, powered, current, and blank — except for tomorrow. Tomorrow is written out in full, in a hand that has your pressure and your spelling.
unwrittenLog.readA: Three rows of route, three names of things that live on them, and the hour you get through. You take the route.
unwrittenLog.readB: Tomorrow is very short. You close the log before the last line and the ship takes the damage anyway, on time.
unwrittenLog.writeOut: You write a quiet day and sign it. Something out here files it. For the rest of the act your repairs land a little kinder.
unwrittenLog.burnOut: The casing alone is worth the trip. Tomorrow still happens; it just stops being anyone's fault.

stormBreak.text: A probability front, three rows wide, walking towards you at the speed of a decision. Inside it dice have no settled faces until something looks at them.
stormBreak.rideA: You come out the far side with a hold full of unsettled faces and a re-roll that reaches one die further.
stormBreak.rideB: You come out the far side. Most of you does. The plating settles into a shape it has not agreed to.
stormBreak.anchorOut: You fix one face and let the front break around it. It costs an hour and takes a step of pressure out of the whole reach.
stormBreak.wait: Sit it out in the lee of a wreck
stormBreak.waitOut: Six hours in someone else's shadow. Boring, cheap, and the hull comes back a little.

secondCaptain.text: Your ship, station-keeping, lights correct, hail correct. In the chair is you — the version that turned back at the Core and has been out here ever since, learning things.
secondCaptain.trade: Trade your worst die for theirs
secondCaptain.tradeOut: «Take it. I remember hating that one.» The exchange is clean, and neither of you mentions how they knew which one.
secondCaptain.warnOut: You tell them everything. They listen properly, which is more than you did, and they leave you their spare plating for it.
secondCaptain.fight: Only one of you gets to be the one
secondCaptain.fightOut: They saw it coming, obviously. They have been rehearsing it for forty years.

borrowedTurn.text: A lender's buoy, Choir make, still solvent. It will advance you time against the ship: a fuller reactor now, a smaller hull to put it in, forever.
borrowedTurn.borrowOut: Three fights open with the bank already full. The hull it came out of does not grow back.
borrowedTurn.repay: Settle the turn you already wrote
borrowedTurn.repayOut: The buoy accepts your own signature back and closes the account. The relief is physical and the plating knows it.
borrowedTurn.declineOut: It does not argue. Lenders out here have all the time there is, and they know it.

lastKeeper.text: The Keeper is here, at the last marker, and has been for a while. «Five,» he says, without turning round. «You did the five. Nobody has done the five since the fleet.»
lastKeeper.carry: Take the marker and carry it in
lastKeeper.carryOut: «Then hold it level.» He says that twice, and the second time it is clearly not about the marker.
lastKeeper.relieveOut: He hands over the log, the key and a die he says was never his. Then he sits down, which he has not done in forty years.
lastKeeper.leaveOut: «Of course.» He goes back to the marker. There is salvage in the shell of the old post, and taking it is easy.

coreRemainder.text: What is left of the Core after the Core: a remainder, roughly the size of a lifeboat, still deciding things at a low volume. It has not noticed you yet, or it noticed you first.
coreRemainder.measurePass: Small, steady numbers. Echo builds a shield lattice off them and the ship comes out of the reading bigger than it went in.
coreRemainder.measureFail: The numbers look back. The whole reach leans a step closer to whatever it is they were measuring.
coreRemainder.keep: Cut it loose and keep it
coreRemainder.keepOut: It fits in the hold. It keeps deciding in there. Echo asks you, once, to reconsider, and then never mentions it again.
coreRemainder.returnOut: You seat it back into the gap it came from. It settles, and something the size of the sector exhales through your hull.

thresholdBeacon.text: The sixth marker was never on the network. It has no message and no owner; it only measures, and what it measures is how far you are leaning.
thresholdBeacon.hold: Hold the needle where it is
thresholdBeacon.holdOut: The needle does not move, which the marker appears to find remarkable. Something acknowledges, at a frequency Echo files and does not translate.
thresholdBeacon.commit: Push the needle to your side
thresholdBeacon.commitOut: You give it a straight answer. It pays like a straight answer: full banks for three fights and a crate of nothing complicated.
thresholdBeacon.walkOut: You leave the needle to itself. The reach relaxes a step, and three more rows come out of the fog on the way past.

wardenInspector.text: A Warden inspection drone clamps itself to your hull and starts scanning your racks. In a quarantine zone probability cores are contraband, and your whole rack is probability cores.

dia.l1: «Declare all cores. Undeclared cores will be confiscated. Declared cores will be confiscated with a receipt.»
dia.l2: It has scanned me twice now, captain. I am choosing not to take that personally.

opt.rewire: Rewire it to scan the lane

out.declare: It confiscates your weakest core and, under a regulation older than the Cut, issues a replacement from evidence stores. Then it stamps your racks and lets go.
out.declareFined: It accepts the declaration, stamps your racks and fines you for filing late. You were late by thirty-nine years.
out.hidePass: It logs a clean hold, stamps your racks and lets go. As far as the Warden's records go, you are nobody in particular.
out.hideFail: It finds the false panel on the second pass, logs you as a smuggler and detaches hard enough to leave a dent.
out.burnOff: It comes off in pieces, and the pieces are Warden-grade alloy. The dent it leaves is yours to keep.
out.burnOffSignal: It comes off in pieces — but one of the pieces finishes its transmission before it stops.
out.rewirePass: Reprogrammed, it spends the rest of its battery scanning the lane ahead instead of your hold.
out.rewireFail: It objects to being reprogrammed — electrically, through your hull.

wardenPicket.text: A Warden picket boat drops into your lane, running lights in the old fleet pattern. It has the inspection drone's stamp on file and would like to see whether you still match it.

dia.l1: «Stamp on file. Hold position for inspection. Inspection is a formality. Formalities are mandatory.»
dia.l2: One gun, one crew, one very long memory. I would rather not test any of the three, captain.

out.submit: They find nothing they have a form for. While the paperwork runs, their tender seals a seam in your hull out of pure habit.
out.submitFined: They find the scrap you did not declare and fine you for it, very courteously.
out.fee: The fee is logged as a fee. The picket marks you inspected, and the sector seems to lose interest in you.
out.feeLogged: The fee is logged as a bribe, and the bribe as a fee. You are cleared, and poorer, in that order.
out.forgePass: Your stamp outranks the drone's. The picket apologises and hands over a confiscated core by way of compensation.
out.forgeFail: The forgery is excellent. It is also issued by an authority that never existed, which the picket notices, and answers.
out.seize: No more formalities. The picket calls in its escort.
out.seizeYield: The crew is two cadets and a recording. They surrender the boat's stores before you finish the threat.

twelfthHull.text: Fleet manifests list eleven ships. Your scope has just found a twelfth hull: fleet pattern, fleet paint, no registry. It faces the same way as every other wreck on the Rim.

dia.l1: I know all eleven by the hum of their reactors, captain. I do not know this one.
dia.l2: Which is strange, because it seems to know me.
dia.l3: Its transponder is dark. Its airlock is standing open.

out.boardPass: Fleet racks, fleet stencils, and one core still seated in a cradle the manifest says was never fitted.
out.boardFail: The airlock cycles you in and then keeps cycling. You leave through a bulkhead you cut yourself.
out.hail: It answers on a channel Echo has no record of. For a moment the lane ahead is drawn in fleet notation.
out.hailSelf: It answers in Echo's own voice, a second ahead of Echo. Echo says nothing else until the next jump.
out.strip: Forty years unmaintained, and not a mark of wear on it. The plating comes away clean.
out.stripBit: The plating comes away clean, but the hull does not want to give it up, and takes it out on yours.
out.mark: You drop a Keeper's marker on it. Somebody whose job is witnessing should witness this.
out.markLit: The marker lights. So does something deep in the hull, briefly, as if answering — and the whole sector hears it.
out.scuttle: A charge in the reactor bay. It goes up like any other hull, which is a relief you did not expect to feel.
out.scuttleTwin: It goes up. A moment later, three rows back, a fleet-pattern hull that was never on your scope goes dark as well.

twelfthWake.text: The twelfth hull is off your stern. Nothing aboard it is running, yet it holds station exactly where a fleet escort would, weapon ports open.

dia.l1: It is flying formation on us, captain. Fleet formation. Nobody taught it that.
dia.l2: I would like to call it a coincidence. I have run the numbers. I would no longer like to call it a coincidence.

out.escort: For two fights it runs ahead and feeds you power on a fleet channel. You open each one already charged.
out.escortBrief: It feeds you power for exactly one fight, then turns coreward without a word, the way the fleet did.
out.answer: It sends back a heading and a single word: «quieter». The lane resolves further than your sensors should reach.
out.answerGift: It sends back a core, across a channel that should not carry matter. Echo will not look at it.
out.shakePass: You burn hard across three lanes. When you look back it is facing the way the wrecks face, and not following.
out.shakeFail: It keeps pace effortlessly and scrapes your hull every time you try to cut across its bow.
out.fire: It does not answer. Its guns do.
out.fireBreak: It does not fire back. It comes apart very neatly along seams it did not have a moment ago, and you collect the pieces.

salvageClaim.text: Two ships reach the same dead freighter in the same minute. Rim salvage law says whoever cuts the hull first owns whatever falls out. The other crew is already lighting a torch.

opt.maraName: Say you are cutting for Mara

out.cutPass: Your torch bites first. By law it is all yours, and by law they are allowed to hate you for it.
out.cutFail: Their torch bites first, and their pilot drifts a little too close to your hull while you argue the point.
out.split: They take the offer and the stern half. Nobody cuts anybody.
out.splitShort: They take the offer, then take the better half while you are still counting.
out.buyOut: You pay them to leave. The freighter's sealed core locker is yours.
out.buyOutPlate: The locker is empty, but the freighter's armour is fleet-grade, and you bolt a plate of it onto your own.
out.maraName: Mara's name clears the lane. The other crew kills its torch and wishes her well, loudly.
out.maraNameCore: They know Mara better than you do. They leave, and leave a core behind for her — «on account».

claimFeud.text: The crew you out-cut at the freighter has found you again. They have brought two friends and a copy of Rim salvage law with notes in the margins.

dia.l1: Their captain reads the law aloud on an open channel, slowly, with feeling.
dia.l2: They have underlined the word «first», captain. Twice, and once in red.

out.fight: The reading ends. The cutting starts.
out.fightFold: Their two friends look at your guns, then at each other, and remember appointments elsewhere. The crew pays you to forget the whole thing.
out.payShare: They count it, grunt, and cross out their annotations.
out.payShareTip: They count it and, grudgingly, mark a clean lane on your chart by way of change.
out.outrunPass: You burn out of reading range before they reach the end of the paragraph.
out.outrunFail: They catch you mid-burn and cut. It is perfectly legal. It is also your hull.
out.pageTwoPass: There is no page two. You read it anyway, with total confidence, and they leave to find a copy — dropping the salvage they came to take back.
out.pageTwoFail: They have page two. It is about ramming.

choirCountdown.text: A Choir buoy is anchored to the spine of a dead tanker, reading numbers aloud on an open band. They are going down. It has been counting for a very long time, and it is nearly finished.

dia.l1: «Every number is an alternative we have closed. Count with us, captain. It gets quieter towards the end.»
dia.l2: I caught myself counting along. I have stopped. I would like you to notice that I have stopped.

opt.giveNumber: Give it the number you heard

out.countAlong: The count settles into the rhythm of your reactor. For the next two fights your cells wake already full.
out.countAlongCalm: The count is soothing in a way you do not like. The crew sleeps properly for the first time in days, and wakes up fixing things.
out.retunePass: It now counts in fleet notation — buoy positions, lane markers. Useful, and a great deal less holy.
out.retuneFail: It resists the retune and plays the count through your own speakers for a full minute. You do not lose your place.
out.cutLoose: It comes away with a lot of good copper in it. The count stops mid-number.
out.cutLooseHeard: It stops mid-number, and every Choir receiver in the sector notices the silence.
out.giveNumber: It skips a thousand numbers at once and drops a core from its housing, as if in thanks.
out.giveNumberBlack: It skips a thousand numbers and hands you a black core, warm, as if it had been waiting for you to ask.
out.recordPass: Echo studies the recording for an hour. The count is the Rim's wrecks, one by one — including the rows you have not flown yet.
out.recordFail: The recorder is not quiet enough. The buoy notices, and reads the rest of the count onto every band.

countCollector.text: A Choir skiff falls in beside you, its hull painted stem to stern with numbers. The newest one, still wet on the stern plate, is the number your count stopped at.

dia.l1: «You counted with us. We have brought you the next number. It is smaller. They are all smaller from here.»
dia.l2: A sermon about subtraction, captain. I would like to know what they are subtracting.

out.takeNumber: They hand it over as a black core, cold, with the number etched on every face.
out.takeNumberCharge: They read it to your reactor instead. It hums the number through the next two fights, and your coils open them full.
out.refuse: They take the refusal as a kind of answer, and open their gunports to correct it.
out.refuseMarked: They take the refusal meekly and paint it on their hull. The whole sector seems to read it.
out.paintPass: You get close enough to paint a zero over the fresh number. The skiff leaves with a very long silence on its band — and a little of its tithe in your hold.
out.paintFail: They see the brush coming, count it as an offering, and answer it with a shaped charge against your hull.

coreSplinter.text: A probability core has burst against a wreck's hull and left itself embedded there as splinters — dozens of them, each one faintly lit.

dia.l1: They are humming, captain. Six different keys, none of them in tune with the others.
dia.l2: I would prefer they hummed somewhere other than my hold. I am told the price outvotes me.

opt.graft: Let a green core graft them

out.pryPass: They come out whole. None will seat in a rack, but the hangar back home knows exactly what to do with splinters like these.
out.pryFail: One splinter comes loose early and answers a question nobody asked. The hull pays for the answer.
out.feed: The reactor drinks them one at a time and runs hot for days. The next three fights open with your cells already charged.
out.feedChoke: The reactor drinks the first handful and chokes on the rest. One charged fight, and a scorched housing.
out.graftPass: The green core roots into the splinters and grows out along your hull like coral, and about as stubborn.
out.graftFail: The green core takes one taste and rejects the graft — violently, through the plating.
out.sell: A salvager on the Rim band pays fair for the coordinates, and does not ask why you are not keeping them.
out.sellHigh: The buyer overpays, badly. You do not correct her.

yusufTariff.text: Yusuf's convoy is parked across the lane, haulers nose to tail. His lead ship is flying a tariff pennant, which as far as you know is not a real thing.

dia.l1: «You taxed my haulers, captain. My accountant says it is only fair that I tax you back. My accountant is me.»
dia.l2: He is enjoying this. I think we should let him have a little of it.

out.pay: He counts it slowly, in front of everyone, and waves you through.
out.payTip: He counts it, then — because he cannot help himself — tells you where the raiders are sitting.
out.holdPass: His haulers blink first. He pays you a tariff to go away, which he insists is completely different.
out.holdFail: His escorts shoulder you out of the lane, and somebody reads your heading out on an open channel. Company is coming.
out.apologize: He hears all of it. He does not forgive you, but his mechanic looks at your hull while he thinks it over.
out.apologizeCore: He says an apology is worth exactly one spare core, and throws one at you. It is a good one.
out.taxAgain: You clip his margins a second time. He does not say anything, which is worse.
out.taxAgainFight: This time his escorts were expecting it.

fieldsMarketDay.text: The Fields' market day has drifted into your lane: forty hulls lashed bow to stern, trading by mass, by story and, as a last resort, by scrap. Mara's stall is at the far end, where the light is kindest to the merchandise.

dia.l1: «Captain. Your hold looks heavy and my table looks light. Let's fix one of those.»
dia.l2: She priced our hull before we finished docking. I'd be flattered if the number were bigger.

opt.swapRail: Put your worst core on the swap rail
opt.tellStory: Sell the story of your last fight
opt.liftCrate: Lift a crate while the stalls are busy

out.swapRail: The rail takes your worst core and hands back a stranger's, plus ten for the difference in mass.
out.swapRailLoud: The core that comes back hums on a frequency the whole market can hear. So can the interference.
out.buyChart: Mara's chart is current to the week, which out here counts as prophecy.
out.buyChartStale: The chart is forty years stale, and one row of it is still true. Mara refunds half, with a short speech about reading before buying.
out.storyPass: Scrap is priced by story here, and yours clears forty. Somebody asks to hear it again from the top.
out.storyFail: The crowd has heard better, but tips you five for effort. One of them follows you out to hear the ending in person.
out.liftCrate: Nobody is watching the crate. Nobody here ever is, until they are.
out.liftCrateCaught: Market security is one tug with a magnet and no sense of humour.
out.standRound: Forty hulls drink to your registry. The clans keep very careful count of who buys.
out.standRoundBrawl: Forty hulls drink to your registry, and two of them settle an old argument across your airlock.

clanTowPledge.text: A clan tug matches your drift and offers the oldest contract in the Fields: if your engines die out here, they tow you home. In return, when they call, you come. Nobody has ever written the terms down. Nobody has ever needed to.

out.pledge: They weld a tow-eye to your keel. It is now the strongest thing on the ship, and it carries their mark.
out.pledgeTested: They weld on the tow-eye and test it the clan way, by hauling you through a debris shoal. It holds. Your paint does not.
out.payDeposit: Scrap is not a promise, but it is a deposit. Their crews patch you whenever you fight inside their range.
out.payDepositOnce: They take the scrap, patch you once, and look at you the way you look at a stranger.
out.inspectPass: You look it over without seeming to. The tug is sound, the crew is sober, and the promise comes with their tow routes.
out.inspectFail: They see you checking their welds. A clan forgives theft twice and rudeness never, and word of this travels faster than you do.
out.stripTug: The cable comes free with the winch still attached, and the clan band starts reading your registry out loud.
out.stripTugFight: The tug was not alone. Its wingmates come about before you have the winch stowed.

towCalledIn.text: Three short pulses on the clan band, then your registry, then nothing. The tug you made a promise to is calling it in. Its tow-eye beacon sits two rows off your course, and it is not moving.

dia.l1: That's them. Engine cold, crew alive, and they spent their last flare on our name.
dia.l2: Something that is not a clan ship is holding station behind the tug, waiting to see what you do.
dia.l3: For the record, captain: nobody would ever know if we didn't come. I would. But nobody else.

opt.passToYusuf: Pass the call to Yusuf's convoy

out.comeFight: You come about. The thing behind the tug turns out to be two raiders who had counted on nobody answering.
out.comeTow: The raiders did not wait. You tow the tug home yourself, which costs plating, and their yard patches you after every fight from here on.
out.sendScrap: It is not what you promised, but it buys them an engine. The clan band logs it as paid, with a note.
out.sendScrapCold: The scrap arrives. They wanted you. The clan band goes very quiet about your registry.
out.passToYusuf: Yusuf sends a hauler without asking why. The tug gets home, and now two ledgers owe you.
out.passToYusufLate: Yusuf's hauler arrives after the raiders did. The clan got itself home, and it remembers who didn't come. Yusuf sends his route notes by way of apology.
out.letItGo: You hold your course and keep the fuel the detour would have burned. The beacon stops pulsing a row later.
out.letItGoHeard: You hold your course. The clan band reads your registry out on every channel, followed by one word.

mineShepherd.text: An old woman in a hardsuit is herding mines. She nudges each one along with a boathook, calls it by the name her grandmother gave it, and keeps the flock drifting clear of the lane. She has noticed that you are in the lane.

opt.hireHer: Pay her to walk you through
opt.learnNames: Learn the names and go slow
opt.waitOut: Cut engines and let the flock pass

out.hireHer: She walks you through by name, mine by mine, and marks three rows of safe lane on your chart while she's at it.
out.hireHerNewMine: One of the flock is new, nobody has introduced you, and it introduces itself against your hull. She apologises to it, not to you.
out.namesPass: You say each name softly and the flock parts. At the far side she hands you the bellwether's old core. «It's retired. It should see something.»
out.namesFail: You mispronounce one. It takes offence the only way it knows how.
out.cullFlock: Forty years of patient mines strip down to very good casing, and only one of them objects. She watches you do it and does not say a word.
out.cullFlockAnswered: The first detonation wakes the clan minelayer the flock was keeping company.
out.waitOut: You cut engines and wait. The flock drifts past, and the lane is quieter for it.
out.waitOutTrailed: You wait out the flock. Something with guns uses the time to catch up.

bargeCount.text: A breaker barge, forty cutters on deck, all singing the count: one metre, two metres, the cut, the cut. The Preacher has come aboard and is teaching them a better tune. The foreman wants him off. Both of them turn to you, since you and the Preacher have met.

dia.l1: «It is the same arithmetic, captain. I only ask them to notice what they are counting towards.»
dia.l2: The foreman says nothing. Forty cutters keep the count without him.
dia.l3: Work songs keep time. Hymns keep people. I know which one I'd rather the cutters had.

opt.singBoth: Sing the count and the hymn together
opt.stripBarge: Strip the barge while they argue

out.backForeman: The Preacher goes without a fuss. The foreman pays you in cut metres, which spend like scrap anywhere in the Fields.
out.backForemanHum: The Preacher goes without a fuss, still singing. The interference in the lane picks up his tune.
out.backPreacher: By the third verse the cutters are counting towards something. Your reactor hums along for a couple of fights.
out.backPreacherFined: The new hymn is lovely. The foreman fines you for the shift it cost him.
out.singPass: You find the beat the count and the hymn share, and forty cutters find it with you. The Preacher hands you a coil and looks, for once, surprised.
out.singFail: You lose the count. So does a cutter arm, which swings wide through your dorsal plating.
out.stripBarge: Nobody is watching the stockpile. Everybody is watching the argument.
out.stripBargeCaught: The barge's breaker drones were not invited to the argument, and were watching the stockpile.

inheritedLedger.text: A clean little cutter at a clan mooring, priced at a third of what it's worth. The seller is keen and keeps glancing at the lane. The catch is bolted to the pilot's seat: the ship's ledger. In the Fields the ledger comes with the hull, and this one owes three clans.

opt.honourLedger: Buy it and pay out the ledger
opt.burnLedger: Buy the hull, burn the book
opt.readLedger: Read the ledger before you buy

out.honourLedger: You pay every line and strip the cutter's armour onto your own hull. Three clans mark you paid, which is worth more than the armour.
out.honourLedgerCore: The armour is rotten through, but there's a core in the seat well and a clan patch crew that owes you now.
out.burnLedger: The book burns fast. The armour bolts on slow. Three clans will be looking for whoever owns that hull.
out.burnLedgerSeen: The book burns fast, and one of the three clans was moored close enough to watch it.
out.readPass: Two of the three debts were paid years ago and nobody crossed them out. You settle the last one, and the cutter's armour is yours for a song.
out.readFail: The ledger is in a clan cipher you read exactly wrong. The mooring charges by the hour, and the hours were long.
out.tipClans: The seller was not the owner. The clans take the cutter back and pay you a finder's fee in front of everyone.
out.tipClansFight: The seller was not the owner, and does not take being found out well.

yusufNameRoute.text: Yusuf's convoy is laid up at a marker buoy, and Yusuf is in a trading mood. Convoy masters never sell a route for scrap. They trade it for a name — a real one, said on the open channel — which the convoy then carries from lane to lane for as long as anyone flies it.

dia.l1: «A route for a name, captain. It's the only price I've ever quoted you honestly.»
dia.l2: He means it literally. Convoys carry names the way we carry cores. Pick one you can stand to hear repeated.

opt.fleetName: Give him a name from the blackbox

out.ownName: He writes it on the convoy board in chalk that doesn't come off. The route he gives you back is good for three rows.
out.ownNameHeard: Every convoy on the band knows your name by the next marker. So does everyone who listens to convoys.
out.echoName: He writes «Echo» on the board. Your reactor runs warm for a couple of fights, which Echo insists is a coincidence.
out.echoNameKnown: Yusuf stops with the chalk halfway. «The fleet had an Echo.» He says nothing else, but his welders come aboard unasked and leave the hull thicker than they found it.
out.fleetName: You read him a name off the recorder you kept. Yusuf knew her. The route he gives you back is his own, and so is the yard.
out.fleetNameCrew: You read him a name off the recorder you kept. He goes quiet, then sends a patch crew over with the route, as if you were the one who'd been hurt.
out.falseName: He writes it down without looking up. The route is good. The name will travel a long way without you.
out.falseNameCaught: Yusuf repeats it back slowly, the way you repeat a name you mean to check. By the next marker he has, and so has everyone he told.
out.offerScrap: He won't sell a route for scrap. He will put it in the convoy's repair fund, and the convoy's mechanics treat you as a subscriber.
out.offerScrapJoke: He takes it for the fuel fund and gives you exactly one row of route, as a joke that is also a lesson.

cutterMind.text: A breaker clan has wired a fleet-era mind into its cutting rig. It measures metres now — nothing else, all day — and when your transponder pings it, it stops measuring and reads out your ship's old fleet designation. Out loud. On every band.

dia.l1: That's one of ours. A navigator, before. They've cut it down to a tape measure.
dia.l2: The clan foreman comes on the channel and asks, reasonably, why his rig has stopped.
dia.l3: I'm not going to tell you what to do, captain. I'm just going to be very quiet until you do it.

opt.buyMind: Buy the mind off the rig
opt.carryOn: Tell the foreman to carry on

out.buyMind: The foreman sells it for the price of a new counter. Echo takes it into a spare partition and closes the door behind it.
out.buyMindNavigates: The foreman sells it for the price of a new counter. It wakes up in your spare partition and, out of habit, starts plotting the lane.
out.talkPass: Echo talks to it on a band nobody else uses. It wakes enough to understand, moves itself into your spare partition, and leaves a shard of its old lattice behind — a gift Echo says will outlast both of us.
out.talkFail: Something in the conversation goes wrong. It reads your fleet designation on every band until the foreman pulls its plug, and everyone in range heard.
out.pullCore: The rig fights for it the way rigs do, with the cutting arm. You come away with a core that still remembers being a navigator. Echo says nothing for two rows.
out.pullCoreFight: The core comes out damaged, and the clan's breaker crew comes out angry.
out.letItRest: Echo asks for a minute first. You give her five. It goes quiet all at once, the way a relay does, and the band in the lane goes quiet with it.
out.letItRestBilled: It goes quiet all at once. The foreman bills you for a new counter, and Echo pays it from your account without asking.
out.carryOn: The foreman thanks you with a cut of the day's metres. The rig starts measuring again. Echo mutes the band.
out.carryOnFollowed: The foreman pays you, and the rig starts measuring again. It keeps reading out your designation until you're out of range, and so does the interference.

yardStrikebreakers.text: The yards have hired strikebreakers: three ripper tugs with fresh paint and no transponders, parked where the picket used to be. Their boss hails you by registry. «You've met the strikers. You know where they sleep.»

opt.bluffBoss: Tell him the strike is already settled

out.sellPicket: He pays on the spot and never asks how you knew. Eleven transponders go dark somewhere behind you.
out.sellPicketHeard: He pays half on the spot. The picket was listening on the same band, and pays you back in its own coin.
out.warnPicket: The picket scatters before the rippers arrive. The yards downstream hear who warned them, and price you accordingly.
out.warnPicketFight: The picket scatters. The rippers work out who warned it and come about for you instead.
out.bluffPass: He believes you, bills the yards for a wasted trip and tips you for the news. The picket never learns how close it came.
out.bluffFail: He checks. It takes him one call. The rippers open with a warning shot that isn't one, and their friends remember your registry.

anchorMassPocket.text: A pocket of dense, slow space the clans call anchor mass. Time runs thick inside it: a hauler went in eight days ago by your clock and has been signalling for what it swears is a year. The mass itself is worth a fortune to anyone who can cut it loose.

dia.l1: I've been in one of these. I think. I remember it as a year, and I remember it as eight days, and neither memory will let go of the other.
dia.l2: The hauler's signal repeats. It has started including the date, in case you have lost track.

opt.cutMass: Cut anchor mass from the rim
opt.mindFlies: Let the freed mind fly the pocket

out.cutPass: The mass comes loose in one dense slab. Bolted to the keel, it makes the hull heavier than it has any right to be, and the offcuts sell.
out.cutFail: The slab shears the wrong way. For a few seconds the stern is a day older than the bow, and the plating did not enjoy it.
out.towHauler: They come out a year older and grateful in a way that lasts. Their captain presses a core on you that she has been saving since spring — her spring.
out.towHaulerAged: They come out. So does your tow line, forty years corroded in eight minutes, and it takes a slice of hull with it when it snaps.
out.mindFlies: The navigator flies the pocket like it has done it before, because it has. It brings you out the far side with the hauler's lost cargo and two rows of lane it remembers.
out.mindFliesSlow: The navigator flies it well, but slowly. You come out with a core from the hauler's hold and a day's worth of interference stuck to the hull.
out.skirtPocket: The pocket soaks up the interference around it, and you ride its wake past, picking up what it has shed.
out.skirtPocketShear: You slide along the pocket's edge. The edge takes a panel, very slowly, and keeps it.

maraTwiceStall.text: Mara's stall is open twice: once off your bow, and once an hour down the lane — same awning, same dent in the same crate. The later one has a sign hung out: CLOSING DOWN.

dia.l1: Don't deal with her. She's me with an hour less patience and worse margins.
dia.l2: Both stalls carry the same stock, captain. One of them has already sold most of it.
dia.l3: I heard that. This deep, I hear everything twice.

opt.playBoth: Play one Mara against the other

out.buyNow: She sells you the good core and watches the lane behind you the whole time, in case she comes back for it.
out.buyNowSecond: The core she meant for you is already gone — the later Mara sold it an hour ago. You get the next best thing, and a patch kit by way of an apology she will deny making.
out.waitForSale: Everything is half price and the hour is full price. You leave with a core, and the sector keeps the hour.
out.waitSoldOut: By the time you get there the stall is sold down to the awning. She gives you the lane charts pinned to it, because she can't take them where she's going.
out.playPass: You quote each of them the other's price until both are underbidding themselves. Neither Mara will ever forgive the other.
out.playFail: They compare notes. It takes them no time at all, being the same person, and both of them sell your heading to the next buyer down the lane.
out.warnHer: She reads the sign for a long moment, then writes you a yard chit and starts packing early. «Tell me how it ends. No — don't.»
out.warnHerDoubt: She doesn't believe you, or doesn't want to. She rewires your damage control for nothing, which is how Mara says thank you for bad news.
out.robLater: The later stall is closing anyway. You help it close. It's the first time you've seen Mara too tired to chase anyone.
out.robLaterCaught: The later Mara is still Mara. You get halfway to the airlock with the crate before the shock-baton finds your hull.

courierNetwork.text: Twelve courier drones hold a ring around a dead buoy, swapping packets faster than you can log them. One of them is running the handshake of the drone you cut out of the mag-net on the Rim. It has been busy.

dia.l1: The ring turns to face you and holds there, every drone at the same polite distance.
dia.l2: It's sending the same thank-you it sent on the Rim, captain. Twelve times over. I think it's proud.

opt.joinRing: Let the ring route through you
opt.askLane: Ask them for a clean lane
opt.netRing: Net the ring and sell the drones

out.joinRing: Your transponder joins the ring. By the next market your name arrives ahead of you, with a discount attached and a little scrap for the carriage.
out.joinRingHot: Your transponder joins the ring, and the first packet routed through you is somebody's bounty notice. The discount is real. So is the company it brings.
out.buyPacket: The packet is a core in a courier cradle, addressed to someone forty years dead. The ring considers the delivery made.
out.buyPacketChart: The packet is a survey of the whole split, kept current by twelve drones that never stop flying it. For the rest of the sector the fog sits further off.
out.askPass: The drones fly the lane ahead of you, one after another, and leave their wake lit. Four rows resolve and the fold is briefly civil.
out.askFail: They show you the lane, but your helm can't hold their pace. Two rows resolve; the hour you lost keeping up does not come back.
out.netRing: Twelve drones fit in one hold. The one that knew you stops transmitting before the hatch closes.
out.netRingScatter: The ring scatters faster than the net closes. You bag four drones and a dent from the one that rammed you — you can guess which.

answeredNotice.text: A message buoy in the Rift is blinking your registry. Somebody has answered the notice you pinned to the board on the Rim. The reply is dated next week.

out.readReply: Whoever wrote it has found what you were looking for, or says so. A heading, three rows of clean plot and a salvage claim clipped to the back that actually pays.
out.readReplyWarning: The reply is three words long and signed with your own registry: «Don't go looking.» You take the advice, this once, and spend the searching hours on damage control instead.
out.writePass: You write back before they have written. The fold carries your answer to them and theirs to you, and somewhere in the exchange a core changes hands.
out.writeFail: Your answer arrives before their question. The fold can't settle the order of things and takes an hour out of yours to think it over.
out.followHeading: The heading ends at a wreck with its hold still sealed. The reply was the salvage, and the salvage was real. So were its edges.
out.followHeadingAmbush: The heading ends at a wreck, and the wreck belongs to the things in the Rift that answer notices.
