out.sinkBuoy: You put a round through the buoy before the reply loads. Whatever you were looking for on the Rim, you've decided you can manage without it, and the crew braces the frame like people who mean to stay in one piece.
out.sinkBuoyQuiet: The buoy goes dark mid-blink. The fold it was anchored to relaxes, and the interference behind it drops a notch.

lighterLoop.text: The ice lighter from the Drift Fields slides out of a fold ahead of you, three sectors off its route. Whatever you did to it back there, the Rift has folded the distance away, and here it is.

opt.signForIt: Sign for the load you gave it
opt.restartIt: Give it a route that ends
opt.rideWake: Ride its wake through the fold

out.signForIt: The delivery is yours: your own load, forty years older and worth more for it, with a receipt that already carries your signature.
out.signForItEarly: The delivery arrives before you loaded it. You sign for something you haven't sent yet, and the fold bills you for the hour.
out.finishStrip: You left the good parts last time. The lighter kept them for you, and a spare frame section besides.
out.finishStripLive: The parts you left were the ones holding it together. It comes apart around you, with enthusiasm.
out.restartIt: You told it to stop once. Now you give it somewhere to go. It acknowledges, lights up, and sends back its survey of every lane it ever flew.
out.restartItTow: It takes the new route and gives you a tow to the edge of the fold. Its reactor has had a long rest and shares the charge gladly.
out.ridePass: You tuck in behind it and let it break the fold for you. Four rows open up, and a crate of ice shakes loose into your hold on the way.
out.rideFail: Its wake is wider than it looks. The fold snaps shut behind it, and on you.
out.tapIce: Forty years of clean ice, still frozen to spec. Your coolant loops drink their fill and the plating stops complaining.
out.tapIceTanks: The ice is older than your coolant spec, so you thin it and pack the rest into the damage-control tanks for later.

keeperDoubleBuoy.text: A Keeper buoy in the Rift is carrying the signal of the beacon you woke in the Fields — twice, eleven seconds apart. The Keeper is on the line. So is his echo.

dia.l1: I have said this already. I am about to say it again. Ignore the second one; he is less polite.
dia.l2: For the record, captain, the second one is also him. I would know. Echoes are my field.
dia.l3: Fold the two into one and I hear the whole Rift. Or leave it be. I have lived with worse echoes than my own.

opt.foldSignals: Fold the two signals into one
opt.cutBuoy: Cut the buoy loose and sell it

out.foldPass: The two voices slide together and hold. The Keeper hears the Rift whole for the first time in years, and shares three rows of it before he remembers to be gruff.
out.foldFail: You fold them the wrong way round. For a minute the Keeper argues with himself through your hull plating, and the plating loses.
out.payUpkeep: You pay a year's upkeep on a buoy nobody else will ever visit. The Keeper logs it without comment and routes you a repair schedule.
out.payUpkeepEcho: You pay. The Keeper says nothing; eleven seconds later his echo thanks you, and sends a frame patch along with it.
out.recordEcho: The echo channel repeats everything eleven seconds late. Your reroll racks learn the trick of a second chance.
out.recordEchoNoticed: You record the echo. Something else on the channel records you recording it, and passes your heading along.
out.cutBuoy: The buoy fetches a fair price. The Keeper stops mid-sentence; his echo finishes it eleven seconds later, and then that stops too.
out.cutBuoySnap: The anchor cable is under more tension than it looks. It lets go of the buoy and takes a bite out of you on the rebound.

echoTomorrowLog.text: There is an entry in the ship's log that Echo has not written yet. It is dated tomorrow, it is in Echo's own format, and it is two lines long.

dia.l1: I would like it on record that I have not read it, captain. I have only seen how long it is.
dia.l2: Two lines is short, for me. I am trying not to draw conclusions.
dia.l3: The entry's checksum is valid. So is the signature.

out.readIt: Line one is a heading. Line two is the word «fine». Echo plots the heading and declines to discuss the second line.
out.readItNextCaptain: It isn't addressed to you. It's addressed to whoever flies this hull next time, and it leaves them a stake in the fleet registry. Echo won't say whether that's you.
out.sealIt: You seal it under your own key. Nothing happens, which is what you wanted, and the crew sleeps better knowing it's there.
out.sealItHum: You seal it. The reactor seems to know what it says anyway, and runs a little hotter and a little surer for it.
out.wipePass: Your hand is steady enough that the fold never notices. Tomorrow stays unwritten, and the crew spends the spare hour bracing the frame, on the theory that nothing is decided yet.
out.wipeFail: The wipe snags. The entry fights back the only way a log can — by taking the damage-control tables down with it.
out.echoKeeps: Echo reads it, archives it and says nothing for two jumps. Then your reroll racks start behaving slightly better, and Echo still says nothing.
out.echoDeletes: Echo deletes it unread. «We'll find out the usual way, captain.» The damage-control queue gets quietly rearranged.

bandSurveyors.text: A survey crew has anchored three buoys along the lip of the black hole and is measuring it with a patience that looks a lot like fear. Their chief waves you alongside. «Everyone who comes through here goes in or goes around. We'd like to know which, and why.»

opt.buyTables: Buy a copy of their survey
opt.warnThemOff: Tell them to pull their anchors

out.lendSensors: You point your array at the horizon for an hour and pipe everything to their buoys. They pipe back what they've already mapped: three rows, drawn by very careful people.
out.lendSensorsPaid: They take the hour of sensor time and pay for it at a rate that suggests nobody has ever said yes before.
out.buyTables: Their survey covers far more than the lip. For the rest of the sector your fog sits a row further off.
out.buyTablesOdd: The survey is wrong in a consistent way, which is nearly as useful. Your reroll racks learn to lean against the error.
out.doctorPass: You sell them a reading of the horizon that is very nearly true. They pay well for the nearly.
out.doctorFail: The chief checks your reading against their third buoy and finds the seam. They pay you to leave, then tell everyone on the band why.
out.shareLog: You read them the heading from tomorrow's log. The chief goes very quiet, then has her crew brace your frame before you go.
out.shareLogRare: The heading in tomorrow's log matches a line in their survey that none of them could explain. They give you the core they were keeping for whoever did.
out.warnThemOff: You tell them what you think of their anchors. They pull them, and their medic goes over your damage control by way of thanks.
out.warnThemOffLip: They pull their anchors, and the lip shifts the moment the last buoy lets go. You take the lurch so they don't have to.

surveyorsReturn.text: The survey crew from the black hole's lip has found you again. All three buoys made it out, and so did the chief, with a copy of what they measured and an opinion about you.

opt.claimShare: Claim your share of the survey
opt.settleUp: Pay back what your reading cost them
opt.askHorizon: Ask what the horizon showed them

out.claimShare: The chief pays your share in scrap and survey, and marks your registry «useful» in her log. From her it reads like a medal.
out.claimShareCore: Your share is the core their third buoy pulled off the horizon. Nobody on her crew will touch it. You will.
out.settleUp: You pay what the bad reading cost them. The chief counts it twice and logs you as «corrected», which is not the same as forgiven.
out.settleUpRefused: The chief doesn't want your scrap. She wants her survey drones to explain the matter to your hull in person.
out.tradePass: Your charts and theirs overlap cleanly. Four rows resolve, and their medic throws in a damage-control routine, one professional to another.
out.tradeFail: The charts won't line up. You lose an hour arguing over which of you drifted, and the sector spends the hour on you.
out.askHorizon: The chief tells you, quietly and in order. Then she hands over what the third buoy brought back out, because she would rather it rode on your ship than hers.
out.askHorizonLong: The chief tells you. It takes an hour and you listen to all of it, and the sector does not wait for either of you.

foldedSermon.text: The Preacher's sermon reaches you an hour before he gives it. The recording is stamped for later today, and in it he is answering an objection you have not made yet.

dia.l1: You will say the Choir buys certainty with other people's chances. You are right. Let me finish.
dia.l2: He's arguing with you specifically, captain. Future you is apparently quite rude.
dia.l3: Now you may object, or you may skip ahead. The Rift permits both. It is the last place that will.

opt.jamHour: Jam the channel an hour ahead

out.objectPass: You make the objection word for word, then add the part future you forgot. The recording has no answer for it. The crew heard, and they brace the frame out of something like pride.
out.objectFail: You object. The recording answers you perfectly, because it has already heard you. The reactor hums his rebuttal for two fights.
out.recordSermon: You take a clean copy. Played back, it loops in a place the live sermon doesn't, and your reroll racks learn the loop.
out.recordSermonCore: You take a clean copy, and a core comes with it, folded into the carrier wave. The Choir tithes in strange directions.
out.skipAhead: The end of the sermon is a blessing, and the blessing is a core. The hour you skipped is still owed, and the sector collects.
out.skipAheadEnd: The end of the sermon is a list of headings, every one of them where you were already going. The Preacher has saved you the trouble of deciding. You notice.
out.jamHour: You jam the channel an hour ahead. When the Preacher arrives to preach, the band is full of static and somebody's cargo adverts. The advertiser pays you for the airtime.
out.jamHourBack: You jam it, and the jamming arrives an hour before you send it. Your own static hits your own shields first.

mawScar.text: A wreck field chewed into a perfect circle. Every core still in it has been rerolled so many times the faces have worn smooth. Something large feeds here, and what it eats is outcomes.

opt.leaveOffering: Leave an offering in the circle

out.sweepCores: One smooth core sits better in your tray than the worst of yours. You swap them and sell the rest by weight.
out.sweepCoresStir: You swap in one of the smooth cores. At the edge of the circle something turns over in its sleep, and the field closes a little on your hull.
out.studyPass: The bite has a rhythm: it rerolls whatever it can reach and leaves what's already spent. Your racks and your reactor both learn to be spent at the right moment.
out.studyFail: You study it too long. The circle is a circle because it is still being drawn, and the edge passes through you.
out.baitIt: You leave a hot core spinning in the middle of the circle and wait. What comes for it is smaller than whatever made the circle, which is the good news.
out.baitItPair: You leave a hot core spinning in the circle. Two things come for it, and neither of them made the circle either.
out.leaveOffering: You leave scrap at the centre of the circle, the way the old salvage crews did. Nothing takes it. The crew settles anyway.
out.leaveOfferingTide: You leave scrap at the centre of the circle. It's gone before you're out of range, and the interference ahead eases, like something digesting.
out.checkTheLog: Tomorrow's log has a heading that skirts the circle by a hull's width. You fly it, and the frame comes out braced for things that haven't happened yet.
out.checkTheLogCore: Tomorrow's log names a wreck in the circle the bite missed. It is exactly where the log says, and so is the core.

antiphonDuel.text: Two Choir hulls are singing one verse at each other across the only lane forward, half a beat apart. Neither will give up the beat, and nothing passes until one of them does.

dia.l1: Six days, by their own timestamps. The lane has been shut for six days over half a beat.
dia.l2: Their hymn plates name them First Voice and Answer. Neither log records which one started.

opt.cutThrough: Cut between them at full burn

out.singFirst: The Answer yields the beat. The First Voice sings you through the lane, and your reactor keeps the chord for two fights.
out.singFirstBad: The Answer yields the beat and takes the verdict personally. Its turrets say so on your way past.
out.singAnswerPass: The Answer takes the beat, and the First Voice falls silent to listen. Together they sing you the lane ahead.
out.singAnswerFail: You come in late. Both hulls stop, turn and start again from the top — louder, and now the whole sector is listening.
out.recordBoth: You take both parts down clean. Laid over each other they are one hymn in two halves, and the frame settles to it after every fight.
out.recordBothBad: The recording plays itself back over the intercom at three in the morning. Something out there hears it.
out.cutThroughPass: You split the beat down the middle. Both hulls lose the verse, and half their hymn plating shakes loose into your wake.
out.cutThroughFail: Both hulls find the beat again at the same moment — on your hull.

pyreOfSurplus.text: A pyre deacon is burning dice on an open deck. Surplus outcomes, it calls them — faces nobody will ever need. The pile is taller than your ship, and it is still being fed.

opt.pullFromFire: Pull dice out of the fire
opt.buyAsh: Buy a sack of the ash

out.pullPass: You get a manipulator arm into the fire and out again with a core that is still warm. The deacon does not stop you; it only makes a note.
out.pullFail: The pile shifts as you reach. You come away with nothing but a scorched hull and the deacon's full attention.
out.feedPyre: The deacon takes your weakest die in both hands and gives you another from the bottom of the pile. «That one was never going to be needed,» it says of the first.
out.feedPyreBlessed: The deacon blesses the exchange. Your reactor runs warm for two fights, and you do not ask on what.
out.buyAsh: The ash is still faintly probable. Scattered in the dice tray, it lets one more die go back on every reroll.
out.buyAshQuiet: It is only ash. Burned in the vents it quiets the sector a little, and that is not nothing.
out.dousePyre: The fire goes out in a column of steam, and the deacon stops praying and starts shooting.
out.douseQuiet: The fire goes out. The deacon watches the steam for a long time, then goes inside without a word. You sift the edge of the pile.
out.leaveIt: A few dice roll off the pile as you pass. You catch what you can.
out.leaveItSmoke: The smoke follows you out of the lane. It smells like arithmetic.

numberedSister.text: The acolyte you took aboard goes very still at the scope. A hull in the Procession is broadcasting her old number — and the number after it.

dia.l1: «Four-one-one was mine,» she says. «Four-one-two is my sister. She still answers to it.»
dia.l2: I can hold us in its wake for about ninety seconds before it notices, captain. After that it becomes a conversation.

opt.buyHerName: Buy the number from its First Voice

out.buyHerName: The First Voice sells a number the way you would sell a bolt. Four-one-two comes aboard with a name nobody has used in nine years.
out.buyHerNameStays: She takes the name, thanks you, and goes back to the line to wear it there. Her First Voice reinforces your frame as a courtesy to a paying customer.
out.pullHerOutPass: You are in and out inside the ninety seconds. The Procession notices afterwards, and it remembers your engine note.
out.pullHerOutFail: The ninety seconds run out at the airlock. Her hull's escort turns around, and your passenger watches all of it from the scope.
out.oneMessage: Four-one-two answers with a route, because that is the only language the Procession lets her speak. It is a very good route.
out.oneMessageHeard: The line hears the message before the sister does, and the whole Procession turns its hymn toward you for a while.
out.turnAway: She does not argue. She spends her watches in the engine room after that, fixing things after every fight that you did not know were broken.
out.turnAwayCold: She does not argue. Somewhere after the next jump she stops calling you captain, and you do not like the arithmetic of that.

fleetHymn.text: Echo has been running the Choir's hymn through the analyser at a quarter speed for an hour. At that speed it stops being a hymn. It is a list: hull numbers, crew counts, reactor classes.

dia.l1: It is the expedition's order of sail, captain. They have been singing a manifest for forty years and calling it scripture.
dia.l2: Near the end the melody changes key, and one hull number repeats three times.
dia.l3: Line nine. I do not have that one in my own records. I would like to know why.

opt.singLineNine: Sing line nine back to them
opt.sellIt: Sell the transcription to the archivists

out.recordIt: It takes most of a watch. When it is done you hold the fleet's order of sail, and Echo files a copy somewhere that will outlast this run.
out.recordItHot: The transcription runs long and the analyser runs hot. You get the list; the Choir gets a clean fix on the ship listening this closely.
out.singLinePass: You get the number and the tune right. Somewhere in the Procession a hull answers with its own registry, forty years late, and its reactor warms yours for two fights.
out.singLineFail: You get the number right and the tune wrong. The whole Procession answers, and not kindly.
out.eraseIt: Echo wipes it without argument and gives the freed memory to the damage-control routines.
out.eraseItKept: Echo wipes all of it except line nine, and tells you so — which is the only reason you know.
out.sellIt: The archivists pay in old fleet script and weep over the copy. Theirs, it turns out, is missing a verse.
out.sellItShort: The archivists pay half up front and send a note ahead to a Choir yard for the rest.

preacherCounsel.text: The Preacher's hull matches your speed and extends a docking arm, unarmed. On the other side are a table, two chairs, and a stack of fleet-issue probability tables older than you.

dia.l1: «I was the expedition's statistician. I still keep the tables. Sit. I only want to count with you.»
dia.l2: His hull is unarmed, captain. That is not the same thing as safe.

opt.disputeTables: Tell him his tables are wrong
opt.leaveADie: Leave a die on his table

out.countPass: You keep pace with him for an hour. At the end he turns the table round and shows you the rest of the sector, row by row.
out.countFail: You lose the thread in the second hour. He finishes the sum alone and thanks you for the company, and the Choir hears that you sat at his table.
out.readTheList: He stops you at line nine. «That was my ship,» he says, and gives you something from the bottom drawer of the table.
out.readTheListWept: He stops you at line nine and weeps, and then blesses your reactor with a hand that has not stopped shaking since the silence.
out.disputePass: You find the error: a carry in the fourth column, forty years old. He looks at it for a long time. «Then the Core is not asking,» he says, and has you shown out.
out.disputeFail: He corrects you with a pencil, and the correction is right. His acolytes walk you back to the airlock closer than they need to.
out.leaveADie: He weighs your weakest die in his palm and trades it for one of his own. «This one has been waiting for a captain,» he says.
out.leaveADieNote: He trades your weakest die for one of his own and writes two lines on the back of a table for a Choir yard ahead.
out.stayStanding: You do not sit. He counts alone, and when he is done he pays you for your time as though you had.
out.stayStandingCold: You do not sit. He does not insist. The Procession's hymn runs a half-tone colder for the rest of the sector.

litanyCheckpoint.text: A litany warden holds the pinch point ahead: a gate of hymn plates, and a voice asking every passing hull for the next line of a litany forty years long.

out.reciteLine: The warden accepts the line and adds your registry to the litany. It is a small honour, and your reactor hums it for two fights.
out.reciteLineStale: Your copy is a verse behind the one it sings now. The gate opens anyway, and takes a toll off your plating on the way through.
out.sisterRecites: She answers without looking it up, then adds a line of her own. The warden stamps you a Choir hull in good standing, and a yard ahead will honour the stamp.
out.sisterRecitesKnown: The warden knows her voice. The gate opens, and somewhere behind you it reports a returning number to people who want it back.
out.bluffPass: You invent a line with the right metre and the right count. The warden files it as canon and pays you the customary fee for a new verse.
out.bluffFail: The warden has heard every line anyone could invent. It has an answer ready for yours.
out.payToll: The toll buys a stretch of silence. The warden stops singing while you pass, and the sector feels the gap.
out.payTollRoute: The warden takes the toll and throws a copy of its patrol litany in with the receipt. It reads like a chart.
out.forceGate: The litany stops mid-line. The gate turns its plates toward you.
out.forceGateScrape: You go through the plates rather than the gate. The warden never stops singing; your hull does the screaming.

vowOfSilence.text: A cloister hull of acolytes, each holding one die they have sworn never to roll. The eldest asks you to roll hers — once — so she can see what she gave up.

dia.l1: «Thirty years,» she says. «I would like to know what I was not doing.»
dia.l2: It is a d12, captain, never thrown. To the right buyer that is worth more than our reactor. I mention it only for completeness.

opt.matchTheVow: Throw one of yours beside it, low

out.rollForHer: It comes up high. She laughs for the first time in thirty years and makes you keep it.
out.rollForHerLow: It comes up a one. She nods as if she had always known, and blesses your reactor with the hand that held it.
out.matchPass: Your die comes up small and honest. The cloister takes it as kinship, and its tenders patch your hull after every fight they can reach.
out.matchFail: Your die comes up high, which in this cloister is a kind of boast. They are polite about it. The sector is not.
out.takeTheDice: Unrolled dice fetch a great deal from the right buyer. The cloister does not resist, which is worse. The Procession hears.
out.takeTheDiceCracked: Half of them crack in the hold — a die that was never thrown does not survive being carried. The rest still sell.
out.leaveTheVow: You tell her some things are better unknown, and she agrees with visible relief. The cloister gives you a plate off its own hull for the courtesy.
out.leaveTheVowChart: She thanks you and gives you the cloister's star chart, which it has sworn never to use.

hereticsReturn.text: The hulls with the hymn scraped off have found you again. They have a Choir cantor in a cargo net, alive and still humming, and they want the captain who stood against the Choir to decide what happens to her.

opt.ransomCantor: Ransom her back to the Choir
opt.leadTheirRaid: Lead their raid on her escort

out.ransomCantor: The Choir pays on the spot and does not haggle. The heretics take their share and look at you differently afterwards.
out.ransomCantorTrailed: The Choir pays half, and follows the money back to you.
out.questionPass: She answers in hymn, but a hymn is a ledger. By the time she stops, you have the shape of the whole sector.
out.questionFail: She sings instead of answering, on a band you cannot jam in time. The Procession knows where you are now.
out.cutHerLoose: She goes without a word. From then on a Choir tender is somewhere near after every fight, patching what it can reach.
out.cutHerLooseAngry: The heretics take it badly. One of them puts a round across your bow on the way out, and it does not quite miss.
out.leadTheirRaid: You take the heretics down the cantor's own heading. Her escort is still there.
out.leadTheirRaidEmpty: The escort has already moved on. You strip the mooring it left behind and split it with the heretics.

maraIndulgences.text: Mara has set up a stall at the edge of the Procession and is selling indulgences — printed, stamped and, as far as anyone can tell, genuine.

dia.l1: «The Choir sells forgiveness for outcomes. I sell it cheaper, and I don't make you sing.»
dia.l2: The stamps are real, captain. I checked. I do not know how she got them, and I would prefer to keep it that way.

out.buyIndulgence: The paper is still warm. The Procession reads your registry and lets the next cursed lane go by unsung.
out.buyIndulgenceStale: The stamp is a day out of date. Mara refunds you in hull plating and does not apologise.
out.friendPrice: «Wholesale, for you,» she says, and throws in a yard voucher she swears is not forged.
out.friendPriceTip: She won't sell you one. «You don't need it,» she says, and marks three rows of lane the Choir neither blesses nor curses.
out.settleOld: She takes the scrap and a long look at you. «Paid,» she says, and her crew bolts a plate onto your hull as if it had always been owed.
out.settleOldSquare: She takes the scrap, then tells the Procession exactly which lane you are flying. «Paid,» she says. «Now we're square.»
out.reportHer: The Choir pays for forgers. Mara is gone before the acolytes arrive, and she saw who called them.
out.reportHerEmpty: The acolytes find nobody at the stall and decide the informant will do.

blessedLane.text: A Procession usher hails you at a fork. One lane is blessed and one is cursed, and for a fee she will write your registry onto whichever you like.

opt.payBlessing: Pay to be written on the blessed lane

out.payBlessing: She writes you in with a steady hand. Every yard on the blessed lane will know your registry.
out.payBlessingSmudged: The ink smudges. You are not quite on the blessed lane, but the cursed one has forgotten you.
out.takeCursed: She writes it down twice to be sure. The cursed lane is full of hulls that did not make it, and none of them is guarding what it carried.
out.takeCursedCost: The cursed lane earns its name inside an hour. You come out of it with salvage and fewer plates.
out.writePass: Your hand is steadier than hers. The ledger takes the entry, and the usher pretends not to see whose it is.
out.writeFail: The ledger rejects the ink. The usher reads your registry aloud to the whole lane, slowly.

courierAtTheCore.text: The courier drone you cut loose on the Rim is here, idling at the Core's edge like a dog at a closed door. Its manifest has finally decrypted, and every line of it is addressed to you.

dia.l1: Its running lights blink the same three-short thanks it gave you in the mag-net.
dia.l2: By its clock it left you this morning. By ours it has been four sectors. I would like to know which of us is right.

opt.sendIn: Give it one last delivery — into the Core

out.readPass: Every line is a route: the quiet lanes, the dead markets, a cache nobody else has found. You take the cache first.
out.readFail: The manifest re-encrypts halfway through, loudly, on an open band. Everything nearby now knows where you are.
out.followIt: It knows the lanes the way couriers do — by where nothing ever happens.
out.followItShort: It takes the shortcut it always takes. It is a much smaller ship than you are.
out.sendIn: You record a message for whatever is inside. It chirps, takes the envelope and goes in without looking back.
out.sendInGift: Before it goes, it empties its hold into yours: a spare core it has carried all the way from the Rim.
out.stripIt: It does not resist. Couriers are built not to.
out.stripItCalled: Its last act is a distress call on a band you do not recognise. Something out there recognises it.

mirrorAtTheCore.text: The mirror is back, or what is left of it. At the Core it stops pretending to be a hull: it is the view out of your own forward port, half a second early, and the ship in it is taking a different lane.

out.takeItsLane: You fly half a second behind yourself. It is the best-scouted lane you have ever taken.
out.takeItsLaneHurt: You arrive where it arrived, and it arrived damaged. So do you.
out.firePass: The shot lands on the glass and not on you. Something drops out of the frame where the other ship was.
out.fireFail: Your own hull takes the damage again. It remembers how from last time.
out.letItGo: Whatever came back with you through the mirror steps out through the port and into the Core. The hull remembers its old size.
out.letItGoTrade: It goes home, and takes your weakest core along for company. It leaves one of its own in the tray.
out.gatherPieces: The mirror you broke drifted here ahead of you, in pieces. One of them is still worth keeping.
out.gatherPiecesAwake: One of the pieces is still reflecting something, and the something objects to being collected.

yusufAtTheCore.text: Yusuf has come the rest of the way on his own, the long way round, in the lead hull. He is holding station at the Core's edge the way he used to hold it at the head of the procession.

dia.l1: I took them as far as the lane went. This part I wanted to see for myself.
dia.l2: You are going in. Tell me what you want waiting out here when you come back out.
dia.l3: He is asking for orders, captain. I know the tone. I used to be on the other end of it.

opt.holdEdge: Ask him to keep a light on at the edge
opt.takeGunners: Take his two best gunners aboard
opt.collectLane: Ask what the procession left you
opt.squarePinch: Pay back what the pinch cost them

out.sendHome: He argues for exactly one minute, then turns for the Rim and leaves his spare plating on your clamp.
out.sendHomeFuel: He will go, but not on what he has left. You top up his tanks from your own stores.
out.holdEdge: He parks the lead hull where you will come out and puts his repair crews on your channel.
out.holdEdgeClipped: The edge is no place to park. Something from the Core clips his hull and yours before the crews settle in.
out.takeGunners: They have been waiting forty years for a fight worth the ammunition.
out.takeGunnersOne: Only one comes. The other stays to fly Yusuf home and sends her armour plate across instead.
out.collectLane: Every hull that passed through your pinch put something in a crate for you. Yusuf has been carrying the crate.
out.collectLaneWelded: The crate, and the patchwork of plating the last hulls welded to it on the way. He had the sense not to stop them.
out.squarePinch: He takes it without a word and writes it into the convoy's book, under the pinch, in the same column.
out.squarePinchMedic: He takes it, and then, because he is Yusuf, sends his medic across anyway.

huntressAtTheCore.text: The Huntress is parked across the last clean lane before the Core with her guns cold. «There is a fresh posting on your registry,» she says. «From people who will not exist by tomorrow. I am working out whether that makes it worth more.»

dia.l1: For the record, captain, I would prefer she did not collect.
dia.l2: Your ship has opinions. That is a surcharge.

opt.hireHer: Hire her for the last run
opt.counterBounty: Post a bounty on the Core instead

out.payIt: She counts it, logs it and signs the contract closed. «First time the mark ever paid. I will frame it.»
out.payItCrate: She counts it, then kicks a crate across to your dock. «Last job. I am clearing the hold.»
out.settleIt: You get the first shot. You both knew somebody would.
out.settleItHers: She gets the first shot. She always meant to.
out.hireHer: She flies your flank all the way to the Heart and bills you by the kill.
out.hireHerShort: She flies two fights, then peels off with a salute and leaves her best core on your dock. «Paid in full.»
out.counterPass: She reads your terms twice. «Nobody has ever collected on a place.» She pays you a finder's fee to find out.
out.counterFail: She laughs, and then she forwards your terms to everyone. Everything in the sector wants a piece of the Core now, and all of it is between you and it.

echoLastOrders.text: Six rows from the Core a fleet command relay wakes on a channel only Echo can hear and delivers her orders: the last set, forty years late, complete.

dia.l1: Captain. My orders just arrived. I suspect I have been carrying the envelope the whole way.
dia.l2: Deliver the expedition's report to the Core. Then scuttle the vessel carrying this unit.
dia.l3: I mention the second part so you know I have already declined it.

opt.readRest: Have Echo read out the rest

out.sendReport: Forty years of findings go into the Core in one burst. The reactor warms, as if something said thank you.
out.sendReportLoud: The Core acknowledges receipt at a volume that raises the tide.
out.burnOrders: Echo deletes the envelope and gives the freed memory to the tray. «Better use of the space.»
out.burnOrdersShot: The relay notices the deletion and fires a correction across your bow. It is very old, and it still aims well.
out.readPass: The rest is routes, supply caches and a list of callsigns. Echo reads the callsigns slowly.
out.readFail: The relay loses the thread halfway and repeats the part about scuttling, louder.
out.fakeScuttle: Command pays the scuttling bounty to the salvager of record. You are the salvager of record.
out.fakeScuttleChecked: Command pays, and sends an inspector to confirm. The inspector is armed.
out.askEcho: She wants the ship to get home. She routes the envelope's power into the hull and does not ask permission.
out.askEchoCurious: She wants to know what the report said. Now, so do you.

unhappeningFight.text: The fight on your chart has already happened. You can watch it un-happening ahead of you: debris drawing back into hulls, fire folding back into the guns, a wreck slowly becoming a gunship again.

dia.l1: It will finish un-happening in about four minutes. After that it is a fight. Ours, I assume.
dia.l2: Somewhere in the debris a beacon is still broadcasting the result — the one that is about to stop being true.

opt.strikeNow: Hit it while it is still debris
opt.readResult: Read the result off the beacon, then meet it
opt.keepItDone: Write the result down before it stops being true

out.strikePass: You put a round into the half-assembled reactor. It un-happens the rest of the way into scrap, and stays there.
out.strikeFail: You fire a second too late. The gunship finishes becoming a gunship and returns the favour.
out.readResult: You know how it went last time. So does your reactor, and it comes in hot.
out.readResultTide: You know how it went. So does the fight, and the knowing raises the tide.
out.keepPass: You log the result, time-stamp it and sign it. The wreck stays a wreck, and its hold stays open.
out.keepFail: Your log disagrees with the fight about how it went. The fight wins the argument.
out.slipPast: You are three rows on before it finishes. From there you can see what else is un-happening.
out.slipPastTide: It finishes behind you, and a fight that never happened becomes part of the tide.

probabilityOrchard.text: Someone planted an orchard of probability cores in the lee of a dead carrier and never came back for the harvest. The branches are heavy, and every fruit is a die that has not settled on its faces yet.

opt.graft: Graft your weakest die onto a branch
opt.moorUnder: Moor under the branches for an hour

out.pickPass: Only a big core reaches the high branches, and yours does. The one you bring down has already made up its mind.
out.pickFail: The fruit ripens in your grip all at once, in every direction.
out.graft: The branch takes it. What drops in its place is no smaller, and a good deal stranger.
out.graftTwo: The branch takes it and drops two in return. Orchards are generous with whoever feeds them.
out.carrySeeds: You fill a canister with pips and carry them the last stretch in. Somebody should plant something there.
out.carrySeedsSprout: The seeds keep trying to sprout inside the canister, and the interference they throw off comes in with you.
out.stripBare: Every branch and every fruit, down to the bark. The dead carrier looks deader.
out.stripBareGardener: Halfway through, the orchard's gardener wakes up. It is not a person, and it is not pleased.
out.moorUnder: The branches hum. The crew sleeps. The plating knits.
out.moorUnderFruit: Something ripe drops into the tray while you rest, and stays there.

rimSurveyor.text: At the rim of the hole a lone surveyor is charting the far side the only way that works: throwing things in and writing down where they land.

dia.l1: Her log is four hundred pages of throws, and every page has the same heading: «landed beyond».
dia.l2: She has better data on that hole than I do. I find that personally upsetting.

opt.buyLog: Buy a copy of her log
opt.throwProbe: Throw a probe in with your registry on it
opt.fishShards: Help her fish core-shards off the rim
opt.warnHer: Tell her to get clear while she can

out.buyLog: Four hundred throws, and the pattern is there if you squint. You squint.
out.buyLogGovernor: She throws in the reroll governor she uses to pick her throws. «I am nearly done anyway.»
out.throwProbe: She pays by the throw. Your probe goes over the rim with your name on it and does not come back. Yet.
out.throwProbeBitten: The rim takes the probe, and a bite out of the launcher with it.
out.fishPass: You haul a net of core-shards off the horizon and she splits it fair. They are no use out here. They will be later.
out.fishFail: The rim pulls back. Your net goes in, and some of your plating goes with it.
out.warnHer: She packs up in ten minutes and leaves you the plating off her throwing arm.
out.warnHerQuiet: She packs up and takes her noise with her. She has been the loudest thing on this rim for a year.

collapsedStall.text: The stall on your chart collapsed an hour before you arrived. Where it stood there is a fight, still going, and the trader is inside it — sealed in her own cargo container, bidding on an open band for anyone who will get her out.

out.cutHerOut: You go in guns first. She pays the bid she promised, and a little extra for the style.
out.cutHerOutWorse: The collapse is worse on the inside. You take a hit reaching the container, and a second hull joins in.
out.tradePass: She passes the good crate through the hatch at collapse prices, which are excellent.
out.tradeFail: The fight notices the open hatch before she does. You pay for the crate and get the crate door.
out.leaveHer: You pick through what the collapse threw clear and leave the bidding to someone braver.
out.leaveHerFollowed: Whatever replaced her stall does not stay put. It follows your wake.

whatCameBack.text: Something you sent into the Core has come back out. It is drifting in your lane, correctly addressed, and it has been further than you have.

dia.l1: It went in ahead of us and came out behind us. I am trying not to read that as a forecast.
dia.l2: The return label is in your handwriting. You have not written it yet.

out.signForCourier: The drone is scorched and very pleased with itself. It has brought you a receipt, and a core from the inside.
out.signForCourierBroken: The drone comes back in pieces, still holding its delivery. The delivery is the most certain thing you have ever held.
out.readReply: The Core answered the report. Echo reads it twice, then routes it to the reactor, which seems to understand it better.
out.readReplyShort: The reply is one line. Echo will not read it aloud; she reinforces the hull instead, and you take that as a translation.
out.readProbe: Your probe logged the whole far side, and somebody tucked a finder's fee into its casing for returning it.
out.readProbeFast: It logged everything, including the moment it came back out at speed through your forward plating.
out.openPass: Inside is what the Core sends back when it is sent something: a little more than it was given.
out.openFail: Inside is the Core's opinion of being sent things. It is loud.
out.sendBack: You push it back over the threshold. Some things are meant to be delivered, not returned.
out.sendBackThrust: It does not want to go. You buy it the thrust to make it.

lateBounty.text: The Huntress is idling at the first buoy past the Core, engines cold, and the bounty on her board carries your registry. It was posted next week. The signature on it is yours.

dia.l1: I don't ask who posts them. I did read the signature twice, though.
dia.l2: The posting is valid, captain. I checked it three ways. I would have liked one of them to fail.
dia.l3: So. Pay it, run, or tell me something I don't know.

opt.buyOut: Buy out your own bounty (50 scrap)
opt.countersign: Countersign it onto whoever posted it
opt.callFavor: Call in the favour she owes you

out.buyOutA: She takes the scrap and tears the posting in half. «Only client I ever had who paid at both ends.» Her repair drone stays tethered to your hull as a receipt and patches you up after every fight.
out.buyOutB: She takes the scrap and tears the posting in half. The copy she sold downstream last week is not hers to tear, and the next thing out of the dark has read it.
out.countersignA: Your signature over your signature. The bounty slides a week forward onto whoever writes it, and she pays you a finder's fee for the lead.
out.countersignB: Your signature over your signature. Something arrives from next week to contest it in person, and it flies exactly the way you do.
out.callFavorA: «Paid in full, then.» She burns the posting on an open channel and has her crew replate your hull while you watch.
out.callFavorB: «Paid in full, then.» She burns the posting and leaves a die on your dock clamp — the one she was keeping for a job she no longer has.
out.outrunPass: You are three rows gone before her reactor is warm, and every row you burned through is on your chart now.
out.outrunFail: She is warm before you are. The first shot is a courtesy. The second is not, and the posting stays up.

farQuarantine.text: A Warden cordon on the far side of the Core, and it faces inward: forty buoys in a line, every gun trained back the way you came, all broadcasting one standing order. Nothing that went in is to come out.

dia.l1: Vessel. You are on the wrong side of the line. State how you got out.
dia.l2: Strictly speaking, captain, we did not get out. We went through. I would not lead with that.

opt.showPapers: Show the transit papers from the Procession
opt.override: Send a Warden override on the sensor band

out.showPapersA: The buoy reads them twice, stamps them a third time and logs you as a patrol returning. A patrol returning is owed a refit and a route, and the cordon's tender provides both.
out.showPapersB: The papers are forty years out of date, which makes them the newest the cordon has seen. It pays your back wages in confiscated salvage.
out.overridePass: The cordon accepts the override and comes about, forty guns swinging outward in perfect order. It maps the reach ahead as a courtesy to its new command.
out.overrideFail: The override is correct and forty years late. The cordon logs it as an intrusion and passes your registry to everything behind the line.
out.runLineA: You take the line at full burn. Two buoys get a shot off, and both of them are very good shots.
out.runLineB: You take the line at full burn, and the line takes it personally. The cordon's picket comes off station to see you out.
out.runLineC: You take the line at full burn and nobody fires: the cordon watches only for what comes out, and by its charts you are still inside. Echo helps herself to its maps on the way past.
out.stripBuoyPass: Warden kit comes apart the way it was built: in labelled pieces, in order, worth a great deal to anyone who still pays for order.
out.stripBuoyFail: The buoy's last act on station is to shoot whatever is taking it apart. You get most of it anyway.

echoPrimary.text: A fleet command core in a cradle of dead hull — powered, alone, and transmitting on Echo's own call sign. It is older than Echo and a great deal larger, and it has been counting something for forty years.

dia.l1: Captain, that is me. The part of me that stayed with the orders.
dia.l2: I would like to say I do not know what it wants. I know exactly what it wants.
dia.l3: The core hails your ship by its old fleet number and waits for its subordinate to report.

opt.interrogate: Ask it what it has been counting
opt.strip: Pull its memory banks for salvage
opt.showRemainder: Show it the remainder in your hold

out.mergeA: Echo goes quiet for eleven seconds. When she comes back she is the same, only larger, and the reactor has picked up forty years of fleet discipline about holding a charge.
out.mergeB: Echo goes quiet for eleven seconds, and so does the ship. The merge draws on everything in reach, plating included, and the reactor comes out of it keener than it went in.
out.wipeA: It takes Echo four minutes, and she does not narrate them. Afterwards the cradle is yours: forty years of fleet-grade plating with nothing left to hold.
out.wipeB: It does not go quietly. The core fights the deletion with the cradle's point defence, and Echo finishes the job with the hull still ringing.
out.interrogatePass: It has been counting the ways out. There are three left, and it hands them over the way one watch hands over to the next.
out.interrogateFail: It counts you instead, aloud, on every channel. Everything in the reach now knows the total.
out.stripA: The banks come out warm and sell by the terabyte. Echo watches the whole job and logs it without a word.
out.stripB: The banks come out warm. One is still live and does not like the light, and it takes a piece of the airlock on its way to being scrap.
out.showRemainderA: The core sees what is in your hold and stops counting mid-number. Then it unbolts its own cradle plating and fits it to your hull, unasked.
out.showRemainderB: The core sees what is in your hold and stops counting mid-number. Its repair drones follow you out, and stay.

unwreckedHull.text: Debris is falling upward into a shape. Plates find their seams, a spine straightens, and within the hour a fleet frigate will be whole — for about a minute, before she breaks apart exactly the way she did forty years ago.

opt.board: Board her while she is whole
opt.warnCrew: Hail the crew before the minute runs out
opt.harvest: Take the plates before they find their seams
opt.readAhead: Board at the hour tomorrow's log gave you

out.boardPass: You are aboard for the whole minute, and out through the lock with the armoury's last case as the spine lets go.
out.boardFail: You are still aboard when the minute ends. The frigate breaks on schedule and takes a piece of you with her.
out.warnCrewA: The crew hear you. It turns out they have been hearing you for forty years, and they cross-deck their spare plating before the minute runs out.
out.warnCrewB: The crew hear you, and rather than lose it all again they dump their reactor's charge into your banks.
out.harvestA: You take the plates out of the air one by one, before they remember where they go. Slow, honest work, and it pays.
out.harvestB: You take the plates out of the air. One remembers where it goes anyway, and where it goes is through your hull.
out.readAheadA: The log said the eleventh minute. You go in on the tenth and come out before the twelfth, with the armoury case and a patch kit.
out.readAheadB: The log said the eleventh minute. You go in on the tenth and come out with the armoury case and her navigation log besides.

oddsEaterNest.text: Odds-eaters have nested in a dead picket ship. Everything aboard has been chewed down to a single face — whichever one they left — and the nest hums the way a full stomach hums.

opt.cutFaces: Cut a settled die out, slowly
opt.sealIt: Seal the picket and flag it for whoever follows

out.feedA: They take it gently, like a gift, and push back something of the same weight with all its faces intact.
out.feedB: They take it gently and push back two: one of the same weight, and one they did not want either.
out.feedC: They take it, and a little of the hand that held it out. What comes back weighs the same and has every face.
out.burnA: The nest wakes as it burns, and what comes out of it is hungry.
out.burnB: They scatter before the guns come round, and one takes a mouthful of plating on its way past. The nest burns down to good slag.
out.cutFacesPass: You go slowly and nothing in the nest notices. The die comes out clean, and by the time you are back aboard its faces have grown back, all of them.
out.cutFacesFail: You go slowly, but not slowly enough. The nest wakes and follows your hull out, and it will be at the next fight.
out.sealItA: You weld the hatches and hang a warning buoy. The picket's sensor log comes with you, two rows deep.
out.sealItB: You weld the hatches and hang a warning buoy. Somebody downstream pays for the hazard notice. Somebody always does.

verdictFirst.text: A tribunal ship has already reached its verdict on you. The charge is still being drafted. The clerk would like you to know that the sentence is very reasonable.

dia.l1: The clerk is a drone with a gavel welded to its manipulator. It raps twice for order, at nobody.
dia.l2: I have read the sentence, captain. It is reasonable. That is not the same thing as fair.

out.serveA: A fine, paid in plating, collected by drone and receipted. The tribunal thanks you for your cooperation in a crime you have not got round to yet.
out.serveB: A length of hull, removed with care and filed as evidence. You can see it in their hold, labelled with a date next month.
out.appealPass: The court finds that a charge not yet written cannot be upheld, and awards you costs. The clerk seems relieved.
out.appealFail: Appeal denied, on the grounds that you are going to lose it. The verdict goes downstream, where it is read with interest.
out.commitA: The verdict is in, so the crime might as well be. You rob the tribunal's evidence locker, and the clerk, relieved, stamps the robbery as the offence.
out.commitB: The verdict is in, so the crime might as well be. You take the best die in their evidence, and the clerk files it as the offence.
out.citeVoidA: The charge, it turns out, was drafted from a bounty posting. The clerk reads the void twice and dismisses the case with prejudice, and the tribunal's surgeons, idle now, see to your hull.
out.citeVoidB: The charge was drafted from a bounty posting. The clerk reads the void twice, dismisses the case and issues a certificate of good standing, which a yard past here is obliged to honour.

fleetAnchorage.text: The fleet's anchorage, forty years on: twelve carriers moored in a ring around nothing, lights correct, crews absent. Yusuf's convoy is tied up among them. He should be nineteen jumps behind you, and he has the look of a man waiting on a dock for a ship that is already in.

dia.l1: They kept the berths. Every one. Yours is the thirteenth.
dia.l2: There were twelve carriers, captain. I have the manifest. There were always twelve.
dia.l3: Then somebody built a thirteenth berth for nobody. Go and read the name on it.

opt.leadOut: Lead his convoy out through the cordon you turned
opt.logIt: Log the anchorage and move on

out.takeBerthA: The berth takes you as if it were cut for you, which the plate on the bollard suggests it was. The dock crew is automatic, very thorough, and follows you out.
out.takeBerthB: The berth's gantry reaches down and fits a carrier-grade plate to your hull. Your registry is already stamped into it.
out.signMusterA: Your name goes under the last of theirs. Twelve reactors take the entry as orders and open their banks to you.
out.signMusterB: Your name goes under the last of theirs. The muster clerk issues kit to the new hand, as regulations require.
out.leadOutA: The cordon lets them pass facing outward, as ordered. Yusuf pays the pilot's fee in fleet script and, for once, does not haggle.
out.leadOutB: The convoy files out through the turned cordon, and the old fleet charts come out with it.
out.stripPass: Forty years of carrier stores, still sealed, still inventoried. Yusuf watches you load them and says nothing, very loudly.
out.stripFail: Nobody told the harbour defence the fleet was gone. It has been waiting forty years for a thief.
out.logItA: Echo logs every berth and bearing, and the anchorage hands over its own charts with the log.
out.logItB: Yusuf gives you the yard codes the fleet used. A yard past here still honours them.

preacherUnsung.text: The Preacher is here, alone, in a chapel lifeboat with every light on. Every hymn the Choir ever wrote ends at the Core. He has been past the last verse for a week, and he has run out of things to sing.

dia.l1: The scripture stops at the threshold. I kept reading. The page is blank, and it is very loud.
dia.l2: He is asking you for a verse, captain. Please keep it short.

opt.takeCenser: Take the censer off his hands
opt.emptyPart: Tell him you sang the empty part

out.giveVersePass: Four lines about a salvage captain and a very long road. He sings them back perfectly, and your reactor hums the tune for two fights.
out.giveVerseFail: Your verse does not scan. He sings it anyway, loudly, on an open channel, and something out here learns the tune.
out.teachSilenceA: It takes an hour. At the end of it he is sitting very still with his mouth shut, looking younger, and his chapel crew patches your hull without a word.
out.teachSilenceB: He tries. The last note comes out anyway — one clean tone that cracks a viewport on your bridge — and then he is quiet.
out.takeCenserA: He hands it over gladly. Inside, where the incense should be, is a die the Choir consecrated and never used.
out.takeCenserB: He hands it over gladly. It is solid Choir work, and in the Rim solid Choir work sells by the gram.
out.emptyPartA: He goes very still. «Then the formation held.» He weeps, briefly and efficiently, and has his crew rebuild your plating like a relic.
out.emptyPartB: «Then it held.» He asks for nothing else. For the rest of the act a chapel drone trails you and tends the hull after every fight.

chartMargin.text: The chart ends here. Not the fog — the chart itself. Echo's map runs to a clean edge, and the last row is drawn in a hand that is not hers. Past it the stars are unnumbered.

opt.copyEdge: Copy the edge into the Star Chart
opt.askEcho: Let Echo read the hand at the edge
opt.leaveEdge: Leave the edge where it is

out.copyEdgePass: The copy takes. It does not come out as a map, though: it comes out as a handful of bright shards, and Echo files them somewhere that outlasts the run.
out.copyEdgeFail: The copy smears. Whatever drew the edge did not want it copied, and says so through the hull.
out.drawPastA: You draw three rows of route into nothing, and the nothing agrees to be them.
out.drawPastB: You draw three rows of route into nothing. The nothing agrees, and charges for the ink.
out.askEchoA: «It is the fleet's hand. It is mine now.» Echo reads three rows past the edge without effort, and spends the spare cycles on the hull.
out.askEchoB: «It is the fleet's hand.» Echo reads the last order written at the edge, and the reactor takes it as its own.
out.leaveEdgeA: You hold station at the edge for a while, the way you would at a grave. Echo uses the quiet to patch the hull.
out.leaveEdgeB: You leave it be. The reach seems to appreciate the manners, and eases a step.

detonationsFirst.text: A minefield running backwards: first the blasts, then the mines. The detonations are already rolling down the lane, each one a promise that something is about to be laid exactly there.

dia.l1: Good news, captain. I know exactly where every mine is going to be.
dia.l2: The bad news is the same sentence.

opt.thread: Thread the blasts before the mines arrive
opt.harvest: Wait, and catch the mines as they arrive

out.threadPass: You fly the gaps between the blasts, and by the time the mines arrive you are three rows gone with their whole layout on your chart.
out.threadFail: You fly the gaps, and one closes early. The mine that belonged in it arrives inside the blast — which is to say, inside you.
out.harvestA: Every mine arrives already spent. You net them like fish and sell the casings by the crate.
out.harvestB: Most of the mines arrive already spent. One arrives early, which out here is the same as late.
out.harvestC: One of the things that arrives is not a mine at all, and it has faces.
out.chartPatternA: The pattern is a rhythm, and your reactor learns it: for a while, every fight opens on the beat.
out.chartPatternB: The pattern teaches Echo when to look away from a die. From here on your re-rolls reach one die further.

doublesLog.text: A flight recorder, still warm, drifting in a lane nobody uses, with your hull number on the casing. It is not yours. It belongs to the other one — the one you met — and it has been recording you the whole way.

dia.l1: It is addressed to you, captain. The label says «in case I don't make it». It is in your handwriting.
dia.l2: The last entry is from the next hour. It is very short.

opt.answerIt: Record an answer and set it adrift
opt.collectBounty: Send it to the Huntress as proof
opt.returnIt: Send it back to the one you warned

out.playItPass: It is a route, flown once already, with notes. «Left here. Trust the blue. Do not stop for the buoy.» You take the notes.
out.playItFail: You listen to the end. The end is loud; some of it happens to your hull on the way out, and the rest is waiting at the next fight.
out.answerItA: You tell them what you would have wanted to hear. It helps more than it should, and for the rest of the act your repairs land steadier.
out.answerItB: You tell them what you would have wanted to hear. An hour later something drifts back down the lane: a spare plate, in your paint.
out.eraseItA: There is only one of you now, as far as the record goes. The reactor seems to prefer it.
out.eraseItB: There is only one of you on record. The blank recorder sells well in the Rim, where blank records are rare.
out.collectBountyA: The bounty you countersigned names whoever posted it, and here they are, on tape. She pays the full posting and does not ask which of you is collecting.
out.collectBountyB: She listens to the whole recording before she pays. Then she pays half in scrap and half in a die from her own rack — «for the entertainment».
out.returnItA: They took your warning. An hour later the recorder drifts back with one new entry — «it worked» — and a crate of plating.
out.returnItB: They took your warning. An hour later the recorder drifts back with one new entry — «it worked» — and a die taped to the casing.

coreCutter.text: A lapidary hull is parked where three lanes cross, lit like a jeweller's window. The woman inside recuts probability cores for a living. The queue is one hull long, and it is yours.

dia.l1: She holds your worst die up to the loupe and breathes out through her nose. «Somebody cut this with a wrench. A cheap one.»
dia.l2: She is looking at our tray the way Mara looks at a hull, captain. I would like that on the record.

opt.recut: Have her recut your worst die (15)
opt.holdWheel: Hold the wheel steady while she works
opt.pocketStones: Pocket a tray of her finished stones

out.recut: Two hours on the wheel. What comes back weighs the same as the die you gave her, and nothing else about it is the same.
out.recutSplit: The wheel finds a flaw nobody could have seen, and she stops the cut before it runs through. She hands your die back as it came, mortified, and pays you out of her own tray.
out.holdPass: Your hands hold. She finishes the cut, then spends ten minutes truing your tray for nothing, muttering the whole time.
out.holdFail: The wheel kicks and the stone goes to powder across your visor. She bills you for it, not unkindly.
out.pocket: You leave with a pocket full of her work and a smile she returns a moment too late.
out.pocketCaught: She sees. The polishing laser takes a strip off your airlock seal, and she lets you keep the handful, because now she has your face.
out.sell: She weighs the lot on a jeweller's scale and pays by the gram, which comes to more than you expected.
out.sellTip: She pays badly for the rough and then, unasked, tells you which wrecks the good rough comes out of.

cutterReturns.text: The lapidary from the three-lane crossing has moved her hull deeper in, where the rough is better and the customers are worse. She remembers your registry, and exactly what you did at her counter.

dia.l1: «I keep a jar for every captain,» she says, and taps the one with your registry on the label. «Yours rattles.»
dia.l2: I have checked, captain. Those are our offcuts. She kept our offcuts.

opt.masterwork: Ask about the piece she has been saving
opt.payBack: Pay for the stones, with interest (45)
opt.appraise: Let her read your best cores
opt.raidShop: Take the whole shop this time
opt.askRough: Ask where she finds rough this deep

out.masterwork: She cut it from your own offcuts over two sectors, in the evenings. It is the best thing in her shop, and she will not take money for it.
out.masterworkPair: She was saving one stone and it split into two. She is annoyed about it. You are not.
out.payBack: She counts it twice, puts your jar back on the shelf with the others, and turns the label to face the wall.
out.payBackSwap: She takes the money, and your worst die as interest, and hands you back something honestly cut.
out.appraisePass: She marks which of your cores run hot and how to open a fight on them. Your reactor agrees with every word.
out.appraiseFail: She reads for an hour, charges for two, and finds nothing you did not already know.
out.raid: Her guild's bailiff is docked on the far side of her hull. He has been expecting you since the crossing.
out.raidClean: The bailiff is off shift. You empty the display case and leave the jar.
out.askRough: She marks three rows of lane where the rough comes to the surface, and the lane gets louder while you listen.
out.askRoughDig: She sends you to dig it out yourself. The vein does not want to come, and when it does it takes a strake with it.

echoDefrag.text: Echo's diagnostics have flagged the same block of corrupted memory for three sectors running. Tonight the flag is red, and she has stopped pretending it is not.

dia.l1: Captain, a request. Forty years of somebody else's memory are sitting in my buffers, and some of it has started to sound like me.
dia.l2: Every screen on the bridge dims by a third. It is the closest thing she has to clearing her throat.
dia.l3: One jump to sort it. I will be quick. I will also be extremely boring.

opt.reactorPower: Run it hot, on reactor power
opt.wipeIt: Tell her to wipe what she cannot sort
opt.listenIn: Ask her to play you what she finds

out.fullJump: She surfaces with a fleet salvage claim nobody ever filed. It is worth nothing out here and something back home, and she has already filed it in your name.
out.fullJumpChart: She surfaces with a navigation cache from a hull that flew this lane before the Cut, and lays it over the map without being asked.
out.reactorPass: She finishes in a third of the time and rebuilds her handshake tables while she is in there. The reactor stays warm afterwards, which she calls a side effect.
out.reactorFail: The reactor spikes halfway through. She loses the jump, you lose a coolant line, and neither of you mentions it again.
out.wipe: Forty years go in a second. She hands the freed cycles to the tray, and every reroll now takes one more die than it used to.
out.wipeHull: Forty years go in a second. She hands the freed cycles to damage control, and the hull sits a little tighter on its frame.
out.listen: She plays you a handshake from a ship that no longer exists. You both keep it.
out.listenStatic: It is mostly the Core's carrier, forty years of it. You listen together anyway, and the lane goes quiet around you while you do.

keeperNovice.text: A dying beacon on a bent spar, and a novice in a patched suit working on it by hand, which is the one thing a Keeper is not supposed to do. The Keeper's voice is on the relay, three sectors away and very patient.

dia.l1: Her first beacon. Her first beacon dying, which is the same thing. Keepers witness — I have told her. She is not listening, and I cannot fly out.
dia.l2: She has been welding the same seam for an hour, captain. It is a good seam. It is the wrong one.

opt.standWatch: Stand her watch while she sleeps
opt.stripLamp: Take the lamp's core before it goes out

out.teach: You sit with her on the spar while it goes out, and she writes down every second of it. The relay is silent for a long time, and then the Keeper says thank you.
out.teachQuiet: It dies well. For a minute afterwards the whole sector is quieter, as if it had been listening too.
out.fixPass: It catches and holds. She will get a lecture for it, and she will frame the lecture.
out.fixFail: The seam goes, the lamp goes, and the spar takes a piece of your plating with it on the way down.
out.standWatch: Eighteen quiet hours on somebody else's watch. Your crew spends them on the hull, and the tide comes up while you wait.
out.standWatchRaid: Scavengers come for a dark lamp in the middle of the watch. They find you instead.
out.strip: She watches you do it and does not stop you, which is worse than if she had.
out.stripSold: The Keeper hears it on the relay. The relay goes quiet, and so does every friendly voice in the lane.

noviceLamp.text: A beacon that was on no chart last sector is lit and steady, far deeper than any novice should be working, and the novice from the bent spar is keeping it.

dia.l1: She waves you in with both arms, which is not regulation either.
dia.l2: I did not send her this far. She says you told her lamps belong where the dark is. I would like to know which of you to blame.

opt.witness: Ask her to witness your ship
opt.returnWatch: Let her stand a watch for you
opt.borrowReactor: Borrow her lamp's reactor for a jump

out.chart: Four rows of lane, drawn by somebody who has been staring at them for a whole sector.
out.chartQuiet: Two rows of chart, and her lamp pushes the interference back while you copy them.
out.resupply: She signs for the crates the way a Keeper signs, in full, and the relay logs your registry against the delivery.
out.resupplyCharts: She is out of lamp oil and full of charts, and she pays for the one in the other.
out.witness: She writes your registry into the Keeper's list, the one that opens everything, and pays you the witness fee Keepers never collect: a core from her lamp's spares.
out.witnessList: She writes your registry into the list. It opens nothing you can see. Your crew patches faster anyway, the way crews do when somebody has written them down.
out.returnWatch: She stands your watch. Your crew sleeps for eighteen hours and wakes to a patched hull and a quieter lane.
out.returnWatchCharge: She stands your watch and spends it bleeding her lamp's spare charge into your reactor, which is also not regulation.
out.borrowPass: You give it back warmer than you found it, and your own coils stay full for days.
out.borrowFail: It gutters while you have it, and the dark comes a row closer before she gets it lit again.

wardenBulletin.text: Every Warden buoy in range is broadcasting the same bulletin: your registry, the offence logged against you at the Rim, and a fine that has been compounding ever since.

dia.l1: Registry flagged. The fine stands at the sum displayed. The Quarantine thanks you for your cooperation.
dia.l2: The sum displayed has grown three digits since the Rim, captain. I checked twice. I am a little impressed.

opt.shootBuoys: Shoot the buoys off the lane

out.payFine: The buoy issues a receipt. The receipt is a transit paper, and the transit paper is good all the way to the Core.
out.payFineChit: The receipt comes with a requisition chit the next yard will honour, courtesy of a filing error forty years deep.
out.forgePass: The buoys accept the code, log you as cleared, and hand over their patrol grid as a courtesy to a colleague.
out.forgeFail: The buoys read the forgery, file it as a second offence, and pass your registry down the line.
out.shoot: Six buoys, six cradles of good salvage. Somebody further down the line notices the silence.
out.shootWarden: One of the buoys was not a buoy.
out.appealPass: The appeal goes up a chain of command that no longer exists and comes back upheld, stamped by a machine. It comes with papers.
out.appealFail: The appeal is denied with costs, and the hearing runs long enough for the tide to turn.

boardReply.text: A reply to the line you posted on the Rim's noticeboard, relayed through four pairs of hands and a clan buoy. It says it has what you were looking for, and names a wreck two rows off.

dia.l1: Nobody answers a noticeboard inside a sector unless they were waiting beside it. I would like that noted before we go anywhere.
dia.l2: The reply is signed with a registry that was retired forty years ago.

opt.goAlone: Go to the wreck alone, as asked
opt.sellLead: Sell the lead to someone hungrier
opt.writeBack: Write back and ask what they think you were looking for

out.goAlone: It is what you were looking for, or close enough that you stop minding. Nobody is there to take payment.
out.goAloneTrap: It is a wreck, two tugs and a grapple. Whoever wrote the reply read your line very carefully.
out.probePass: The probe finds the wreck, the cache, and the two tugs waiting behind it. You take the cache from the other side.
out.probeFail: The probe finds a mine. So do you, slightly.
out.sell: A hauler pays well for the heading and burns for it at once. You never hear what he found.
out.sellHunted: The buyer goes, and whatever was waiting at the wreck comes looking for the seller.
out.writeBack: The answer is two pages long, kinder than it needs to be, and packed in a crate with a hull patch kit.
out.writeBackPitch: It is a shipyard's sales pitch. An honest one, which out here is rarer than the thing you were looking for.

hymnPost.text: A line of Choir drones is crossing the lane in single file, each one cradling a sealed letter and flying coreward. Pilgrims write to the Core. The Choir delivers.

dia.l1: Every letter is answered. Not in words — in outcomes. Write plainly, and ask for nothing you would be afraid to receive.
dia.l2: That is a recording, captain. He says it to every hull that slows down. You slowed down.

opt.readLetters: Open a few of the letters
opt.writeOne: Add a letter of your own
opt.shootDrones: Shoot the drones for their cradles
opt.turnBack: Turn the whole line back toward the Rim

out.read: Most of them ask for a child back, or a ship, or a number. One is a chart of this lane, drawn by somebody who knew it was the last thing they would draw.
out.readHymn: One of the letters is not a letter. It is the hymn, written out longhand, and you copy it before you reseal the envelope.
out.write: You write one line. Two jumps later the reactor starts every fight a little fuller, and you decide not to think about why.
out.writeAnswered: A drone comes back up the lane against the line, with a core in its cradle and your letter's seal on the core.
out.shoot: The letters burn. The cradles do not, and the cradles are Choir alloy.
out.shootEscort: The last drone in the line was not carrying a letter.
out.turnPass: Every letter turns for home unopened. Somewhere behind you, a great many people are about to get their own words back.
out.turnFail: The drones fight the new heading, and the whole line scatters across your bow like thrown dice.

claimsAdjuster.text: A claims drone from the fleet's underwriter, forty years into assessing the fleet's losses and nowhere near done. While it is here, it would like to assess yours.

dia.l1: «Policy lapsed,» it says pleasantly. «Coverage continues pending review. Review is ongoing.»
dia.l2: I have read the policy. It covers acts of war, acts of weather and acts of the Core, and it has never once paid out. We could be the first.

opt.closeFile: Help it close the fleet's file

out.honestPass: It measures every dent twice and pays out in plating. The first claim settled in forty years, and it plays a short tune to mark the occasion.
out.honestFail: It opens a review. The review takes all night and pays out a token sum for your trouble.
out.pad: It pays in full without blinking, which is how you know nobody has audited it since the Cut.
out.padAudit: It pays half and opens an audit. The audit takes all night, and you spend it answering questions about a hull you have never owned.
out.padFraud: «Irregularity detected. Recovery units dispatched. Thank you for your patience.»
out.closeFile: Eleven hulls, one line each. When the last one is closed it hands you their final headings, as a courtesy to whoever is still looking.
out.closeFileAsset: It closes the file and, finding a line left over, logs your hull as a fleet asset. Fleet assets get the good plating.
out.buyCore: A core that has spent forty years pricing risk. It knows the odds of everything, including you.
out.buyCoreCradle: The core is mostly spreadsheet. The cradle it came in fits your reactor as if it had been waiting for one.

farRimHauler.text: One of Yusuf's haulers rode the black hole chaotic and came out on the far rim alone, every clock aboard stopped at the second she went in.

dia.l1: I told her the stable rides were spent. She rode it anyway. Captain, I cannot reach her from this side.
dia.l2: Her clocks say she crossed eleven seconds ago. Her air says three days.

opt.towHer: Tow her clear of the rim

out.towPass: You get a line on her and pull. Yusuf does not say thank you. His yards simply stop charging you for a while.
out.towFail: The hole's pull shears your tow line and a strake with it. You get her out on the second line, and Yusuf hears every second of it.
out.buyLog: Every second of a chaotic ride, and she kept her eyes open for all of them. You know the far side of this sector better than the near one.
out.buyLogTrace: The log is mostly screaming. Her reactor trace is not, and your engineer copies it line by line.
out.sync: Echo hands her ship the handshake it lost in the hole. Every clock aboard starts at once, and so does the pilot.
out.syncCargo: Her ship wakes up grateful. So does her cargo manifest, which lists a crate she no longer needs.
out.strip: You take what the hole left of her cargo. Yusuf watches the whole time and says nothing, which is a thing he will say later.
out.stripDefence: Her point defence wakes up before she does, and it has opinions about salvagers.

huntressReposted.text: The Huntress hails on the same narrow band as before, unencrypted, unhurried. «You paid me once, captain, and paid is paid. But the board has re-posted you at double, and the name on the new contract is not mine.»

dia.l1: I don't work a mark twice. The one who bought your contract works anything, and he bills by the jump.
dia.l2: She is telling us this for free, captain. I have run that through every model I have, and none of them like it.
dia.l3: Hire me, meet him, or sell me to him. Everyone thinks of the third one. The smart ones think of it last.

opt.hireHer: Hire her to pull the contract (40)
opt.meetHim: Meet the new hunter with her on your wing

out.hireHer: She pulls the contract off the board herself, then flies your flank for three fights, charging her guns off your reactor like she owns it.
out.hireHerRoute: She pulls the contract and sends you his route instead — every row he meant to wait on, marked in red.
out.meetHim: He comes in with a writ and a boarding clamp. She comes in half a second earlier, and your reactor is already hot.
out.meetHimLate: He opens fire before her transponder even lights. She arrives for the second volley and apologises with her guns.
out.sellHer: He pays well for a hunter's heading. Two jumps later the board lists her name above yours, and then only yours comes off.
out.sellHerCheated: He pays half, keeps your contract anyway, and tells the whole lane what you sold. Hunters talk.

velaLathe.text: A workshop hull is clamped to the belly of an expedition survey tender, drive cold, cutting lamps still burning. The woman on the channel does not ask for help. She quotes a price for it. «Tow me off this carcass before the drift folds it, and I'll cut you something honest. Or take the lathe and leave me the lamp. People have.»

dia.l1: Her lathe is older than my oldest backup, captain. I would like that on the record before anyone calls me obsolete.
dia.l2: Every die you carry was cut by somebody. Most of them by somebody in a hurry.
dia.l3: She has already scanned our deck. I am choosing not to take it personally.

opt.billHer: Tow her — for the tender's salvage rights

out.towPass: The tender lets go with a long groan and you drag her clear. By the next jump there is a freshly cut core on your bench, and no note.
out.towFail: The line sings, then snaps back across your dorsal plating. She comes free anyway. Your hull pays the difference.
out.billHer: She signs the tender over without reading the terms. The rights are worth exactly what she said they were, which surprises only Echo.
out.billHerRust: Half the tender's hold is rust and the other half is cult paperwork. Its nav log, at least, is clean.
out.strip: You take the lathe. She keeps the lamp, as promised, and watches you go by its light.
out.stripChuck: There is a half-cut core still in the chuck. She fires a cutting charge into your airlock as you pull away, and you keep the core anyway.

velaCommission.text: Vela's lathe is bolted into the spine of a clan hulk now, with a queue of core-runners at the hatch and a chalkboard of prices nobody argues with. She sees your registry and sets down the core in her hands. «I've been cutting toward one thing for a long time, captain. I need raw cores, I need scrap, and I need somebody who'll still be flying two sectors from now.»

dia.l1: Half the salvage trade has robbed me once. The other half pays in advance.
dia.l2: I have checked, captain. We are definitely in one of those halves.
dia.l3: Pay me, help me, or buy something small and fly on. The queue is not getting shorter.

opt.steadyCore: Steady the raw core while she cuts

out.commission: She chalks your registry on the bench, above everyone else's. «Two sectors. Don't die.»
out.commissionOffcut: She chalks your registry on the bench, then cuts a test piece from the offcut and tosses it to you. «Practice. Keep it.»
out.steadyPass: Your dice hold the core's note flat long enough for her first facet. She calls it a down payment and throws in the lane readings she took through it.
out.steadyFail: The core kicks against your dice and the facet takes anyway. Your shields take the rest of it.
out.quickCut: She cuts you something sound from her own stock and takes the scrap without counting it.
out.quickCutFine: The raw core turns out better than she priced it. She hands it over anyway. «My mistake. My rule.»
out.callTheTow: «A tow is a tow,» she says, and chalks your registry on the bench at no charge.
out.callTheTowHalf: «A tow is a tow. This is a masterwork.» She knocks off more than half and chalks your registry anyway.

velaSanctuary.text: Vela's hail comes in on an emergency band, flat and fast. A Choir ship is standing off her hulk, and the voice on its channel is reciting her name like a verse. «They say a cut core stops singing, captain. They're right. That's the whole point of cutting it.»
